sequencing: Complete the full engine through R12 before starting XLR8; owner instruction 2026-10-17.

cards.title: Bootstrap the engine repository and durable project record
cards.deliverable: Create the engine workspace, package/service boundaries, local commands, architecture decision directory, development plan, handoff record and machine-readable progress ledger. Reserve interface packages for consumers and examples without conference imports.
cards.acceptance: A fresh checkout builds the minimal SDK and example with documented commands. Every planned card has an ID, owner lane, dependency and truthful planned status; repository ownership and distribution policy are recorded.
cards.tests: Run the clean-checkout build and package import smoke check; validate progress schema and reject application imports in engine packages.
cards.security: Exclude credentials and source assets from accidental publication. Record dependency trust boundaries and repository protection settings.

cards.title: Establish CI evidence and the merge procedure
cards.deliverable: Add scoped build, unit, integration, browser, migration and security jobs, shared fixtures, artifact retention and a reproducible acceptance record keyed to commit and environment. Document separate self security review followed by required checks and merge verification.
cards.acceptance: A deliberately failing required check blocks acceptance. A changed commit invalidates prior review/check evidence. Progress distinguishes implemented, verified, merged, deployed and release-qualified work.
cards.tests: Exercise passing and failing workflow fixtures, stale-evidence rejection, test sharding and deterministic artifact naming.
cards.security: Use minimal workflow permissions, pinned actions and secret redaction; untrusted pull-request code cannot receive deployment credentials.

cards.title: Define shared contracts and qualification fixtures
cards.deliverable: Define versioned runtime, asset, world, media, identity and service interface contracts. Select canonical meters/axes and prepare test architecture, animated creature, screens, movable props and four audio corners. Establish reference device and workload manifests.
cards.acceptance: The same fixtures and scripted interactions can run against either candidate foundation. Thresholds, feature requirements and evidence formats are fixed before comparative results are reviewed.
cards.tests: Validate manifests, schema compatibility fixtures, coordinate transforms and scripted scenario reproducibility.
cards.security: Use redistributable synthetic fixtures for CI and protect privately obtained originals in controlled test storage; fixture provenance does not constrain product import capabilities.

cards.title: Qualify Hubs and Spoke as a complete foundation
cards.deliverable: Build a reproducible Hubs/Spoke evaluation branch or isolated package using pinned sources. Exercise imported venue, avatar, object manipulation, shared media, browser editing, export/reload and headset entry; record components retained and required changes.
cards.acceptance: Publish runnable evidence against F03 requirements, an extraction/deployment assessment and concrete adaptation estimates. Feature claims without exercised behavior remain unverified.
cards.tests: Run the common desktop/two-client scenario and actual-headset checklist; capture frame timing and reconnect behavior without claiming production capacity.
cards.security: Inventory covered licenses, exposed services, default access policies and stale dependencies; document necessary patches rather than imposing marketplace feature restrictions.
external: An actual target headset for comparative XR evidence

cards.title: Qualify Babylon and reusable VRSpace subsystems
cards.deliverable: Build the equivalent F03 evaluation using Babylon and candidate VRSpace client subsystems. Test scene authoring, avatars, media surfaces, spatial audio, physics integration and portable world state. Record reusable modules and server coupling.
cards.acceptance: The evidence is directly comparable with F04. The proposed combination demonstrates the critical interactions and identifies functionality still requiring implementation.
cards.tests: Run the same desktop, multi-client and headset scenarios; inspect bundle size, frame cost and service boundaries.
cards.security: Check client/server separation, dependency notices, untrusted media routes and credential handling. Do not import an entire service stack merely to obtain a small client module.
external: An actual target headset for comparative XR evidence

cards.title: Select the foundation and map retained subsystems
cards.deliverable: Record the foundation decision against capability coverage, adaptation effort, graphics, operations and maintainability. Map every remaining card to reuse, adapt or implement. Keep one runtime foundation; retire the losing production path while retaining its evaluation evidence.
cards.acceptance: All required outcomes remain assigned. A Hubs selection may retain its working networking/media/editor systems; it does not force replacement by the default libraries. Reused functionality closes a card only after its acceptance checks pass.
cards.tests: Validate the capability mapping, full dependency graph and a build of the selected foundation.
cards.security: Document software obligations and patch ownership. Preserve full import, editing and export goals and an application-independent engine boundary.

cards.title: Pin upstream components and establish fork maintenance
cards.deliverable: Create only necessary source forks; otherwise pin upstream packages and service images. Record source versions, patches, notices, software bill of materials and update responsibilities. Define regression checks for upstream upgrades and supported toolchain versions.
cards.acceptance: A clean build resolves the recorded dependency set and can identify the source of every shipped binary. Local modifications have a reproducible patch or branch history.
cards.tests: Rebuild from lockfiles and verify artifact provenance, license inventory and an example dependency update/revert.
cards.security: Review build scripts, supply-chain exposure and distribution obligations, including native converter builds. No secret or private asset enters a package by default.

cards.title: Establish the engine control API and data services
cards.deliverable: Implement host-injected identity, tenant/project namespaces, scoped capabilities and basic control API middleware. Add durable schema migrations, object-store/queue interfaces, idempotent job contracts and a local service stack. Keep product roles in the host application.
cards.acceptance: A standalone host can create a scoped workspace and call engine APIs without conference records. Two tenants cannot access each other; retries preserve one result and failed migrations recover predictably.
cards.tests: Run real database, object-store and queue integration tests plus authorization, token expiry, migration rollback/forward and idempotency cases.
cards.security: Apply transport encryption, secret isolation, least-privilege service grants and explicit processing trust boundaries; do not claim participant-held encryption for server-readable simulation data.

cards.title: Version complete world, entity and prefab schemas
cards.deliverable: Extend foundation contracts into versioned world, entity, prefab and asset-reference schemas, including component extension points, stable identifiers, hierarchy, source coordinates and migration hooks. Map the selected foundation into these contracts instead of introducing a second scene model.
cards.acceptance: A fixture containing nested prefabs, negative scales, media references and behavior data validates and round-trips without losing identity. Unknown optional components survive preservation; unsupported required components produce actionable errors. Meters, right-handed axes and Y-up remain invariant.
cards.tests: Exercise malformed references, parent cycles, duplicate identifiers, schema migration and coordinate round-trips against independent fixtures.
cards.security: Bound nesting, component sizes and numeric ranges; reject prototype-polluting keys and unresolved external references before instantiation.

cards.title: Implement runtime lifecycle and injectable local services
cards.deliverable: Expose create, load, start, suspend, resume, unload and dispose operations around the chosen runtime. Provide injectable asset, authorization, persistence and transport interfaces with local implementations. Separate scene state from rendering resources and host application UI.
cards.acceptance: A minimal world starts without a conference account, application API or media server. Loading another world cancels obsolete work and disposes previous resources. Repeated mount/unmount and suspended-tab recovery leave one active frame loop and consistent lifecycle events.
cards.tests: Run lifecycle integration tests covering cancellation, failed loads, late asynchronous results and repeated mounting; inspect retained resource counts.
cards.security: Local mode grants only its explicit local capabilities; absent host authorization must never silently authorize a remote world.

cards.title: Load canonical assets into the selected renderer
cards.deliverable: Connect published asset manifests to the selected renderer, reusing its glTF, material, lighting, animation and texture facilities. Support dependency resolution, loading placeholders, cancellation, shared-resource ownership and documented advanced renderer extensions without rebuilding the upstream rendering pipeline.
cards.acceptance: The reference scene loads meshes, textures, lights and animation clips with preserved transforms and source diagnostics. Repeated instances share eligible resources, while disposing one instance leaves others intact. Required unsupported features fail visibly instead of silently disappearing.
cards.tests: Compare representative render fixtures and test missing textures, corrupt resources, cancelled loads, negative scales and shared-resource disposal.
cards.security: Load only authorized manifest resources; enforce resource ceilings and prevent renderer plugins from fetching arbitrary asset URLs.

cards.title: Provide desktop, touch and accessible action input
cards.deliverable: Add application-neutral action bindings for movement, look, selection, interaction and cancellation across keyboard, mouse, touch and gamepad. Provide remapping, focus ownership, pointer-lock lifecycle and accessible equivalents for essential non-spatial controls.
cards.acceptance: Users navigate and select objects with desktop or touch controls without triggering movement while typing. Pointer-lock refusal, focus loss, orientation changes and device disconnection recover predictably. Host UI can consume an action without depending on renderer internals or conference roles.
cards.tests: Use browser interaction tests for input capture, remapping, focus transitions, touch gestures and stuck-key prevention; verify keyboard-only operation manually.
cards.security: Validate incoming synthetic actions through the same bounded action contract; user gestures cannot bypass remote permissions or object capabilities.

cards.title: Integrate WebXR sessions, controllers and comfort controls
cards.deliverable: Adapt the selected foundation's WebXR session and controller support into shared input actions, reference-space handling and session lifecycle. Implement snap turning, teleport requests, seated/recenter controls and optional smooth locomotion with explicit comfort settings.
cards.acceptance: Capability detection exposes only available entry modes. A supported headset enters, exits, recenters and resumes without duplicate inputs or displaced world scale. Session denial and controller loss return usable controls. Locomotion requests remain subject to later collision and authority validation.
cards.tests: Combine mocked session/error tests with recorded physical-headset checks for controller profiles, reference-space resets, sleep/resume and comfort settings.
cards.security: Tracking stays ephemeral by default; XR availability never grants movement, editing or media capabilities.
external: Physical WebXR headset and controllers for acceptance.

cards.title: Add VR-safe controls and qualified hand interaction
cards.deliverable: Provide reusable XR panels, readable prompts, focus states and interaction targets for controller rays and direct selection. Add hand-tracking adaptation where supported, with pinch/debounce handling and controller or desktop fallback; reuse qualified upstream UI components.
cards.acceptance: Users can dismiss errors, adjust comfort, select objects and leave the session inside the headset. Essential controls do not depend on invisible HTML overlays. Hand/controller switching does not duplicate activation, and unsupported tracking preserves a complete interaction route.
cards.tests: Test focus and action routing automatically; verify target reach, text legibility, hand occlusion, accidental pinches and device switching on actual hardware.
cards.security: UI visibility is independent of authority; repeated or spoofed activations still pass object capability and rate checks.
external: Qualified hand-tracking headset for the advertised hand profile.

cards.title: Bridge collision assets and fixed-step physics
cards.deliverable: Implement the selected physics bridge, defaulting to Rapier, for static, kinematic and dynamic bodies, collider manifests, mass properties, collision filters, contacts and transform interpolation. Expose a headless simulation interface suitable for local and authoritative hosting. Use independent collider fixtures first; A13 subsequently supplies production-derived geometry.
cards.acceptance: Architectural openings remain traversable while floors and walls are solid. Physics owns simulated transforms; rendering interpolates without altering authority. Repeated loads release bodies and shapes. Fixed-step behavior is bounded under frame stalls without claiming universal cross-platform deterministic lockstep.
cards.tests: Exercise stairs, arches, negative-scale assets, thin barriers, falling bodies, contact events and frame stalls using independent geometry fixtures.
cards.security: Reject malformed collider data, excessive body counts, invalid numeric values and unbounded catch-up simulation.

cards.title: Implement character traversal, seating and safe teleportation
cards.deliverable: Build a capsule-based character controller with walking, slopes, steps, ground detection, seating, configurable participant collision and validated teleport destinations. Connect shared input and comfort actions while keeping tracked headset motion distinct from virtual body constraints.
cards.acceptance: The traversal fixture supports stairs, ramps, doorways and moving platforms without falling through unloaded collision. Invalid teleports fail clearly. Removing a floor triggers a safe recovery. Real head movement remains tracked; boundary feedback handles wall penetration without forcibly moving the camera.
cards.tests: Run reproducible traversal scenarios plus headset checks for seated scale, recentering, wall approach and interrupted teleport requests.
cards.security: Bound speed, acceleration, teleport range and spawn choices; authoritative validation can replay the same movement intent contract.
external: Physical headset for tracked-camera boundary and seating acceptance.

cards.title: Implement object manipulation, throwing and joints
cards.deliverable: Define reusable interaction intents and control-lease state for selecting, grabbing, carrying, placing and throwing dynamic objects. Implement local physics constraints and bounded joints for doors, levers and attached props, using desktop and XR interaction adapters.
cards.acceptance: A statue can be carried, placed or thrown with predictable release velocity and collisions. Jointed doors obey limits. Losing input, deleting an object or suspending a session releases control safely. The same command/result contract can be hosted by the network authority.
cards.tests: Exercise heavy/light props, fast release, collision during grabs, joint limits, simultaneous local requests and interrupted interactions.
cards.security: Enforce interaction distance, object capability, force and velocity ceilings; imported properties cannot create unlimited constraints.

cards.title: Connect physics interactions to room authority
cards.deliverable: Bind movement and manipulation intents to the authoritative room service with lease arbitration, acknowledgments, local prediction, correction and remote interpolation. Reuse the selected networking primitives; keep shared body ownership separate from collaborative document state.
cards.acceptance: Two clients contesting one object receive one valid owner. Late joiners see current poses, joints and control state. Packet delay, duplicate messages and disconnects produce bounded correction and lease release. A client cannot tunnel, teleport or launch objects by submitting unchecked transforms.
cards.tests: Run two-client browser scenarios and headless fault tests for delayed commands, stale leases, replayed releases and prediction reconciliation.
cards.security: Review all client-controlled movement fields; validate principal, instance epoch, object scope and replay handling before accepting state changes.

cards.title: Integrate navigation meshes, routes and world transitions
cards.deliverable: Integrate Recast/Detour or the qualified reused navigation subsystem for tiled walkability, path queries, off-mesh connections, NPC routing and portal destination contracts. Invalidate impacted navigation regions when geometry changes and expose rebuild status to the runtime.
cards.acceptance: Routes pass through real doorways and avoid blocked or unloaded regions. A removed bridge invalidates affected paths and safe spawn recovery works. A portal resolves a destination without assuming conference sessions; remote authorization and transition orchestration remain host-service responsibilities.
cards.tests: Compare paths against independent obstacle fixtures; exercise disconnected islands, stale tiles, moved blockers and cancellation during transitions.
cards.security: Bound pathfinding work and destination requests; reject unauthorized destination references and malformed navigation links.

cards.title: Load generic avatars and a qualified VRM adapter
cards.deliverable: Create an avatar resource contract for skinned glTF, morph targets, skeleton mappings, body bounds and attachment sockets. Adapt VRM where qualified and preserve unsupported metadata for export. Reuse existing avatar loading rather than imposing one hosted avatar vendor.
cards.acceptance: Multiple independently sourced fixture avatars load at correct scale with stable bone references and valid bounds. Unsupported rigs return useful diagnostics or a safe placeholder. Replacing an avatar disposes resources without changing participant identity or losing host capabilities.
cards.tests: Cover differing bone names, absent optional bones, morph targets, oversized skeletons, malformed skin indices and repeated avatar replacement.
cards.security: Enforce texture, bone, morph and material budgets; avatar metadata and extensions must not execute embedded code.

cards.title: Add avatar animation, retargeting and emote playback
cards.deliverable: Provide animation state machines, clip libraries, blending, root-motion policy and qualified skeleton retargeting. Define generic locomotion, seating, gestures and emote actions with authored fallback mappings rather than assuming every humanoid shares one rig.
cards.acceptance: Compatible fixture rigs play walking, seated transitions and several emotes without scale drift or losing foot contact beyond the agreed tolerance. Unsupported retarget mappings are reported. Interrupting an emote returns smoothly to locomotion; root motion never bypasses the physics controller.
cards.tests: Check clip transitions, missing clips, loop boundaries, different frame rates, root offsets and retargeted reference poses.
cards.security: Bound animation events and clip resource use; event markers invoke approved actions instead of arbitrary code or privileged commands.

cards.title: Add avatar presence, inverse kinematics and attachments
cards.deliverable: Map available head and hand poses onto avatar bones using qualified inverse kinematics, calibration and bounded fallback poses. Add wearable/held attachment sockets, local source offsets and capability adapters for optional face/body tracking without requiring that hardware.
cards.acceptance: An avatar follows tracked head/hands at the configured scale, while absent tracking produces a stable fallback rather than invented measured poses. Attachments remain aligned through animation and avatar replacement. Local and remote pose contracts distinguish tracked, estimated and unavailable data.
cards.tests: Exercise seated calibration, tracking loss, arm reach limits, controller changes and attachment motion on fixture rigs and hardware.
cards.security: Minimize tracking retention and bound pose updates; attachment assets retain ordinary ownership and resource restrictions.
external: Physical headset for head/hand calibration and optional tracking claims.

cards.title: Implement animated wildlife and reusable NPC behaviors
cards.deliverable: Add reusable path-following, flying-route, idle and scheduled-behavior components for non-humanoid actors. Bind imported clips, simple interaction bounds and entity-attached audio while separating shared behavior timing from locally evaluated skeletal animation.
cards.acceptance: A rigged bird follows a route, changes clips and carries its sound emitter without requiring human bone names. Lower-detail clients preserve its authoritative location and behavior. Missing optional audio or clips produces a documented fallback; authored routes stay within configured bounds.
cards.tests: Use synthetic animal fixtures for clip timing, route loops and LOD changes; inspect one actual animated wildlife asset before claiming fidelity.
cards.security: Cap active actors, route complexity and event frequency; decorative actors cannot acquire participant or editor privileges.
external: A usable rigged animal asset for the final fidelity check.

cards.title: Add terrain tiles and environmental scene components
cards.deliverable: Implement versioned terrain tiles, heightfield/mesh rendering and collision bindings, plus reusable sky, water and bounded weather components. Reuse renderer facilities and material presets; keep environmental simulation and quality policy independent of conference venue themes.
cards.acceptance: A tiled landscape loads without visible or physical cracks at approved borders. Terrain edits invalidate affected collision/navigation revisions before traversal resumes. Water and weather have lower-cost fallbacks, and disabling decorative effects leaves navigation and world state unchanged.
cards.tests: Exercise neighboring tile seams, origin/scale conversions, terrain replacement, unloaded boundaries and reduced-effects rendering against reference fixtures.
cards.security: Bound tile size, update frequency, particle counts and environmental parameters; malformed height data cannot exhaust memory or destabilize simulation.

cards.title: Provide declarative object behaviors and trusted extensions
cards.deliverable: Implement versioned triggers, conditions, timers and approved actions for doors, exhibits, object interaction and simple games. Supply a documented trusted-plugin interface and renderer escape hatch while preserving behavior metadata in the world manifest.
cards.acceptance: A fixture game uses interaction, timed events and state transitions without conference code. Behaviors run in the correct local or authoritative context, survive save/reload and handle entity deletion. Cyclic trigger graphs stop at declared execution budgets with useful diagnostics.
cards.tests: Exercise event ordering, timer cancellation, graph cycles, missing action providers and replay after restoring a world revision.
cards.security: Authorize every privileged action, constrain event amplification and keep imported script text inert unless an explicitly supported runtime admits it.

cards.title: Qualify and integrate isolated creator scripting
cards.deliverable: Select and integrate an isolated creator-code runtime with an explicit capability bridge, bounded execution, controlled storage/network access and termination, plus an optional browser script-editor panel. Keep trusted engine plugins separate. Document supported language/runtime versions, execution locations and serialization of script state.
cards.acceptance: A creator-authored object performs useful logic through approved APIs and survives revision export/reload. Infinite loops, excessive allocation and unauthorized host calls terminate without taking down the world. Browser/server differences are explicit; a worker alone is not accepted as isolation.
cards.tests: Run adversarial scripts, cancellation, upgrade compatibility and capability-revocation cases in the actual selected isolation mechanism.
cards.security: Complete a separate escape/broker review covering ambient credentials, origin access, imports, resource ceilings and authoritative command validation.

cards.title: Implement scene streaming and adaptive quality budgets
cards.deliverable: Connect asset variants and spatial cells to projected-size LOD, culling, instancing, staged loading and bounded animation updates. Add separate rendering, memory, transfer and decode budgets with manual quality settings, downgrade hysteresis and gradual recovery.
cards.acceptance: A low-power profile reduces decorative detail while preserving presentation readability, authoritative geometry and usable movement. Collision arrives before entry into streamed regions. Repeated quality changes do not oscillate, leak assets or duplicate entities; premium source variants remain available.
cards.tests: Replay representative camera routes under bandwidth and frame-load limits; inspect resource counts, variant selection and collision-before-traversal ordering.
cards.security: Enforce world and client budgets despite hostile asset metadata; quality selection must not bypass content authorization.

cards.title: Harden renderer selection and graphics recovery
cards.deliverable: Implement capability-based backend selection and recovery around the chosen foundation: conservative WebGL2 immersive entry, qualified WebGPU paths and controlled scene reconstruction. Handle context/device loss without conflating graphics resources with world state or media connections.
cards.acceptance: Unsupported XR/backend combinations offer a working fallback before entry or reconstruct predictably. Simulated context loss restores the current world without duplicate physics or audio. Failed restoration exposes a recoverable user action while preserving independent meeting connections where possible.
cards.tests: Exercise capability matrices, denied sessions, resource recreation, backend changes, headset sleep and repeated device/context loss on supported profiles.
cards.security: Recreated resources recheck authorized manifests; recovery cannot revive revoked assets, stale grants or superseded world instances.
external: Actual target browsers and headsets for each advertised backend profile.

cards.title: Ship independent offline and multiplayer game examples
cards.deliverable: Publish a local physics playground and a small multiplayer game using only released engine interfaces. Demonstrate loading, movement, collision, object rules, reset/save and host-provided identity without importing conference routes, account models, agendas or presenter roles.
cards.acceptance: The offline example works with network access disabled after its packaged assets load. The multiplayer example joins an engine world service directly and supports two interacting clients. Both examples use the same contracts and document deployment/configuration without hidden conference dependencies.
cards.tests: Run import-boundary checks, offline browser tests and a two-client game flow including save/reset and reconnection.
cards.security: Use explicit demonstration permissions; sample credentials and permissive development settings must not enter published production defaults.

cards.title: Qualify runtime performance and supported device profiles
cards.deliverable: Run integrated runtime qualification with representative venues, actors, avatars and media. Publish supported device/backend profiles, reproducible scene versions, p95/p99 frame timings, memory/decoder observations and outstanding fidelity limits rather than one unqualified frame-rate claim.
cards.acceptance: Each advertised profile sustains its selected desktop or headset target and preserves traversal, essential controls and readable presentations. Low-quality fallbacks and graphics recovery work during active media. Failures narrow the published claim and produce corrective work before that profile is accepted.
cards.tests: Replay camera/interaction workloads on actual laptops and headsets, varying active avatars, animals, screens and network conditions independently.
cards.security: Review telemetry for sensitive tracking/media leakage and confirm resource ceilings remain effective during overload and recovery.
external: Reference laptops/headsets and approved representative venue/animal assets.

cards.title: Implement persistent inventories and object ownership
cards.deliverable: Add application-neutral inventories, object ownership, prefab instances, pickup/stow/drop operations and equipment/attachment slots. Persist item identity separately from shared render assets and connect state changes to authoritative capabilities and revisions.
cards.acceptance: A player can collect, carry, store, equip and re-place an object across reconnects without duplicating its identity. Shared venue props and personal items follow distinct ownership rules and remain usable by non-conference examples.
cards.tests: Test concurrent pickup, reconnect during transfer, duplicate retries, destroyed items, attachment replacement and persistence restoration.
cards.security: Check item, inventory and world capabilities at every transfer; clients cannot mint items, seize another inventory or export private dependencies by changing ownership metadata.

cards.title: Asset revisions, preserved sources and converter contracts
cards.deliverable: Define versioned asset, source-bundle, dependency, conversion-recipe and diagnostic schemas. Register importer/exporter adapters with explicit format, version and feature declarations. Preserve original bytes, companion files, authoring coordinates, names, pivots and hashes independently of derived runtime outputs. Provide application-neutral catalog and operation contracts.
cards.acceptance: An uploaded source receives a stable revision and can be retrieved byte-for-byte after a derived revision changes. Capability declarations distinguish native import, exchange import and export without marketplace-specific feature restrictions.
cards.tests: Round-trip schema fixtures, malformed dependency graphs, source-hash verification and recipe-version migration prove identity preservation and compatibility failures.
cards.security: Check tenant ownership on every source, dependency and revision operation; reject ambient filesystem references.

cards.title: Resumable intake for files, folders and archives
cards.deliverable: Implement browser and API intake for individual files, folder selections, drag-and-drop directories and supported archives. Stage a dependency bundle with relative paths, checksums, multipart/resumable progress, cancellation and expiration. Preserve companion textures and nested directories; identify archives by signatures rather than extensions.
cards.acceptance: A network interruption resumes verified chunks without restarting the complete upload. Folder and archive submissions retain equivalent dependency paths, and canceling removes only the intended incomplete session. Unsupported archive types produce actionable results.
cards.tests: Exercise interrupted and repeated completion, duplicate filenames in different folders, Unicode paths, mobile file selection, oversized entries and corrupt chunk hashes.
cards.security: Bind upload tokens to one tenant/session; enforce quotas, path containment, bounded entry counts and safe archive expansion limits.

cards.title: Isolated conversion jobs and recoverable execution
cards.deliverable: Run pinned converters in disposable workers with durable jobs, leases, checkpoints where supported, cancellation, bounded retries and structured progress. Separate staged sources from writable outputs. Record actual tool versions and build inventories. Implement process termination, cleanup and terminal failure classification.
cards.acceptance: A real conversion job survives worker loss through a safe retry and publishes at most one result. A canceled or timed-out job stops its subprocesses, releases its lease and leaves original data intact.
cards.tests: Kill workers before and after output commit; inject queue redelivery, disk exhaustion, malformed parser input and converter hangs. Verify resource accounting and cleanup.
cards.security: Use nonprivileged isolation, no ambient credentials, restricted filesystem/network access and CPU, memory, disk and wall-time limits.

cards.title: Canonical glTF and GLB ingestion with feature validation
cards.deliverable: Implement glTF/GLB loading through the selected runtime and canonical compiler path. Validate buffers, references, skins, clips, morph targets, materials and supported extensions. Normalize source coordinates once while retaining original conventions and stable sub-object identifiers. Publish an explicit extension/fidelity matrix.
cards.acceptance: Representative static and animated fixtures render with correct scale, orientation, hierarchy and materials. Required unsupported extensions prevent a false success; optional approximations remain visible in diagnostics. A valid small GLB can preview before hosted optimization finishes.
cards.tests: Use Khronos fixtures plus mirrored transforms, interleaved buffers, sparse accessors, missing textures, invalid numeric values and oversized allocations; compare rendered reference views.
cards.security: Bound decoded resources and resolve only authorized bundle dependencies; never execute asset-provided code.

cards.title: Immutable publication, reusable results and asset lifecycle
cards.deliverable: Publish immutable manifests and derivative objects atomically, keyed by source hashes, tool versions and complete recipes. Add catalog lookup, asynchronous job-result retrieval, CDN delivery, original retrieval endpoints and reference-aware lifecycle management. Support rebuilding with new recipes without rewriting older worlds.
cards.acceptance: Concurrent identical jobs converge on one valid published result; changing any meaningful recipe input creates a distinct revision. Worlds remain pinned to their selected assets. Unreferenced outputs can be reclaimed without deleting active world or export dependencies.
cards.tests: Exercise interrupted publication, duplicate completion, cache invalidation, expired delivery grants, concurrent references, deletion races and restoration from retained originals.
cards.security: Authorize every catalog and byte-delivery request; prevent cross-tenant existence leaks and unsafe shared-cache keys.

cards.title: OBJ, MTL, COLLADA and legacy 3DS conversion
cards.deliverable: Add qualified OBJ/MTL, DAE and legacy .3ds adapters using pinned open-source tools. Preserve supported geometry, object grouping, transforms, texture references and basic material properties. Record tested exporter variants and supported animation features. Keep .3ds distinct from native .max scenes.
cards.acceptance: A folder containing an architectural OBJ, its MTL and textures becomes an editable runtime asset. A DAE venue retains its hierarchy and openings. Missing dependencies produce specific repair instructions, and static OBJ never claims to preserve skeletal animation.
cards.tests: Convert exporter-diverse fixtures with relative texture paths, negative scale, differing units, transparency, large indices and unsupported DAE features; inspect reference renders.
cards.security: Disable XML external entities and reject escaped paths, excessive nesting and unbounded material/mesh counts.

cards.title: FBX meshes, skins, morphs and animation clips
cards.deliverable: Qualify ufbx and the selected Blender route against the same corpus, then implement the better supported FBX adapter. Preserve hierarchy, units, pivots, skins, blend shapes, clip ranges and supported material bindings. Report constraints, expressions or shader features that require evaluation in the source application.
cards.acceptance: Binary and ASCII FBX fixtures load as the same animated characters at representative poses. Clip names and duration survive conversion, and a file needing native baking cannot silently become a static success.
cards.tests: Compare skinned poses, morph weights, inverse bind transforms, loop seams, reflected coordinates and multiple animation takes against exported references. Include malformed and truncated FBX inputs.
cards.security: Use isolated parsing with allocation limits; embedded media and external references remain within the authorized source bundle.

cards.title: Native Blender scene conversion
cards.deliverable: Implement a version-qualified headless Blender adapter for .blend sources using trusted pipeline scripts. Resolve bundled textures and linked libraries, preserve supported geometry and animation, and identify unsupported node, modifier or driver behavior. Record the exact Blender build and conversion settings in every result.
cards.acceptance: Supported .blend scenes produce editable runtime assets with correct objects, clips and appearance. Sources requiring missing libraries or unsafe embedded execution report the issue without losing originals or automatically enabling scripts.
cards.tests: Run real Blender conversions covering packed/unpacked textures, linked assets, modifiers, geometry nodes within the supported subset and animations; compare outputs and expected failure diagnostics.
cards.security: Disable embedded autoexecution, isolate subprocesses and limit dependency resolution; inventory distributed Blender scripts and binaries.

cards.title: USD family composition and conversion
cards.deliverable: Add version-qualified USD, USDA, USDC and USDZ intake through Blender/OpenUSD tools. Resolve declared references, payloads and selected variants within the source bundle; convert the documented mesh, hierarchy, material and animation subset. Preserve source composition metadata and report every unsupported semantic.
cards.acceptance: A packaged USD scene with local references converts reproducibly using an explicit variant selection. Missing payloads and unsupported curves, volumes or materials appear as identified issues rather than an apparently complete empty asset.
cards.tests: Compare composed transforms, instancing, selected variants, time samples and material references against native source inspection; exercise broken references, cycles and archive faults.
cards.security: Block arbitrary filesystem or network resolution and custom resolver/plugin execution; bound composition depth and expanded resource size.

cards.title: STL, PLY and 3MF geometry classification
cards.deliverable: Implement tested STL, mesh-PLY and 3MF conversion with geometry, color, assembly and unit handling appropriate to each format. Classify point-cloud and Gaussian-splat PLY schemas explicitly and dispatch them to their specialized adapter status. Offer scale calibration when the source omits units.
cards.acceptance: Ordinary geometry imports at the chosen physical scale with preserved supported colors and assemblies. A splat or point file is never misreported as a broken triangle mesh. Users can inspect and correct unknown-unit assumptions before placement.
cards.tests: Use ASCII/binary STL and PLY, colored meshes, 3MF assemblies, mixed-schema PLY, degenerate faces, missing units and malformed container relationships.
cards.security: Apply shared archive containment, XML safety and decoded vertex/face limits; reject nonfinite coordinates and oversized declared counts.

cards.title: Material and animation baking with fidelity reports
cards.deliverable: Build shared baking recipes for supported materials, UV preparation, textures, animation resampling, skin/morph outputs and named clips. Separate source evaluation from runtime encoding so native connectors can contribute evaluated data later. Preserve original high-quality assets and record approximations, missing renderers and deformation losses.
cards.acceptance: Procedural fixtures within the supported subset produce stable PBR outputs and animated clips. Unsupported renderer or rig features produce a correction-required result; static exchange geometry never substitutes silently for a promised animated asset.
cards.tests: Compare reference views, UV seams, normal orientation, feather silhouettes, clip endpoints, morph deformation and baked transform poses using real supported toolchains.
cards.security: Execute only trusted recipes; imported expressions or scripts cannot run outside qualified isolated source-application evaluation.

cards.title: Mesh, texture, LOD and spatial-cell optimization
cards.deliverable: Generate device-tier derivatives using glTF Transform, meshoptimizer and KTX/Basis tooling. Separate byte compression, mesh simplification, texture resizing, material consolidation, instancing and spatial partitioning. Preserve artist-provided LODs and stable entity/sub-object mappings; record recipe-specific resource and quality statistics.
cards.acceptance: A large venue streams nearby cells and appropriate LODs without loading its full detail first. Animated assets retain valid skins and clips across tiers. High-quality sources remain available, and all rendering variants refer to the same authoritative object locations.
cards.tests: Measure transfer, decoded memory, draw calls, geometric error, texture artifacts, LOD transitions and animation deformation on fixed fixtures; prove cache invalidation when recipes change.
cards.security: Cap expansion and optimization work; validate compressed outputs and prevent shared-buffer corruption or oversized GPU allocations.

cards.title: Derived colliders, navigation and safe placement data
cards.deliverable: Generate separate collision and navigation artifacts from normalized geometry. Use simplified static meshes or suitable primitives for venues, bounded convex compounds for movable props, and authored overrides where needed. Preserve doorways, arches and courtyards; produce walkable areas, teleport surfaces, interaction bounds and safe spawn candidates.
cards.acceptance: The reference venue remains traversable without passing through walls or enclosing its interior in one convex hull. A throwable statue uses stable bounded collision geometry. Collision readiness is distinct from visual readiness for streamed cells.
cards.tests: Exercise doorway clearance, stairs, thin floors, concave props, mirrored scale, missing geometry and collider simplification error through the reference controller and physics adapter.
cards.security: Enforce collider complexity and decomposition time limits; reject unsafe spawn data and unbounded navigation generation.

cards.title: Unified browser import, diagnostics and preview workflow
cards.deliverable: Connect the shared drop target to editor placement, immediate placeholders, progress, cancellation, preview generation and repairable diagnostics. Display detected formats, units, missing dependencies, clip/material coverage and resource estimates. Support replacing dependencies and rerunning a recipe without duplicating the intended object. Integrate A25 remote URL sources into the same import progress, diagnostics and publication flow.
cards.acceptance: A user drops a venue, sees truthful progress, checks scale and traversal, then places repeated props. Ready GLBs preview quickly; large scenes remain usable while processing. Failed or canceled imports leave no ghost scene entities or lost originals.
cards.tests: Run desktop and supported headset upload/placement flows, reconnect during processing, cancel/delete races, dependency repair and repeated completion events; compare thumbnails with runtime output.
cards.security: Authorize import-to-world attachment separately from upload; sanitize diagnostics, filenames and preview metadata shown in the browser.

cards.title: Original retrieval and interoperable scene export
cards.deliverable: Expose complete original-bundle retrieval and an export adapter registry with GLB/glTF and a documented OBJ subset. Export selected objects or supported scene snapshots with stable metadata sidecars and explicit feature-loss reports. Document and test foreign-engine exchange-export intake without treating native project containers or scripts as interchange.
cards.acceptance: Users retrieve identical originals and export editable supported geometry, materials and animation without supplier-specific product restrictions. Reimported exchange files preserve their documented subset; engine-only behaviors are identified for complete-bundle export.
cards.tests: Reimport exported scenes in this engine and an independent compatible viewer; verify transforms, names, materials, skins and clips. Exercise foreign-engine-produced exchange fixtures.
cards.security: Check export scope and dependency access; strip session credentials and never execute source-project scripts during intake.

cards.title: Complete world bundles and editable round trips
cards.deliverable: Export and reimport versioned world bundles containing the manifest, dependency graph, assets, optional originals, terrain, prefabs, colliders, navigation, behaviors, media/audio bindings and revision metadata. Provide explicit portable-source inclusion and external-media references. Implement schema migration, collision-safe clone mapping and transactional import.
cards.acceptance: An exported world opens in a clean workspace with preserved stable IDs, editable relationships and essential behaviors. Clone mode remaps references consistently. Live credentials are replaced by explicit reconnect requirements, while file-backed content remains portable.
cards.tests: Compare semantic snapshots and interactive behavior after export/reimport; exercise migrations, missing dependencies, duplicate IDs, partial upload and rollback after late validation failure.
cards.security: Verify bundle integrity and access scope; treat imported behaviors as untrusted data until the behavior system authorizes activation.

cards.title: Qualified native SketchUp connector
cards.deliverable: Implement a version-qualified SKP connector using an actually provisioned supported native SDK or application route. Preserve geometry, components, instance transforms, materials and dependency metadata within the declared subset. Expose qualified native export capabilities through the adapter registry; keep DAE exchange as an independent usable route.
cards.acceptance: Real SKP fixtures convert through the deployed native toolchain and compare correctly with source views. A DAE workaround or mocked connector cannot mark native SKP import accepted. Unavailable native software reports its provisioning dependency accurately.
cards.tests: Run native component, nested-instance, texture, units and version fixtures; exercise actual process failure and unsupported source-version diagnostics.
cards.security: Isolate native execution and validate source dependencies and generated output.
external: Provisioned SketchUp SDK/application access and supported deployment rights; real native fixtures are required for acceptance.

cards.title: Qualified native Maya rig and scene connector
cards.deliverable: Implement MA/MB conversion through provisioned version-qualified Maya workers. Evaluate supported rig constraints and expressions, bake named clips and deformation, resolve dependencies, and export tested exchange/runtime outputs. Integrate shared baking and diagnostics while retaining original scenes and documented source-renderer requirements.
cards.acceptance: A real complex animated Maya fixture preserves its expected clips, feather or attachment motion and supported material appearance. Artist-provided FBX remains useful independently but does not satisfy native MA/MB acceptance. Missing plugins or licenses produce explicit dependency failures.
cards.tests: Compare native sampled poses and reference renders with converted clips; test multiple takes, source-version mismatch, missing plugins and worker interruption.
cards.security: Constrain native script evaluation inside disposable workers without secrets or arbitrary external access.
external: Provisioned supported Maya installation, necessary renderer/plugins and deployment rights; actual native conversion runs are mandatory.

cards.title: Qualified native 3ds Max scene connector
cards.deliverable: Implement native .max conversion through a provisioned supported 3ds Max worker and qualified exporter. Resolve scene dependencies, supported modifiers and instances; bake supported renderer materials and export documented runtime features. Record exact source/application/plugin versions and preserve originals.
cards.acceptance: A real architectural MAX scene becomes a correctly scaled, grouped runtime venue with verified materials and openings. Legacy .3ds or seller-provided OBJ/DAE conversion does not falsely complete native MAX support. Unsupported plugin evaluation remains an explicit technical result.
cards.tests: Compare source views, instance transforms, material assignments and modifier output; exercise missing renderer, unsupported file version, cancellation and native application crashes.
cards.security: Isolate native scene evaluation, restrict file/network access and validate generated resources before publication.
external: Provisioned supported 3ds Max platform, required renderer/plugins and deployment rights; real MAX files and native runs required.

cards.title: Qualified native Cinema 4D connector
cards.deliverable: Implement a Cinema 4D connector through a provisioned supported native application or SDK route. Qualify generators, instance hierarchies, materials, animation and dependency resolution before claiming each feature. Feed evaluated results into the shared compiler and export registry, preserving original scene data.
cards.acceptance: Real C4D fixtures produce matching supported geometry and animation through the deployed toolchain. Generic parser success or exchange-file conversion cannot establish native C4D completion. Missing renderers, generators or unsupported versions produce identified diagnostics.
cards.tests: Run native instances, generator evaluation, animated transforms, material references and missing-plugin cases; compare source views and output pose samples.
cards.security: Run native evaluation with bounded privileges, resources and dependency access; verify output integrity before publishing.
external: Provisioned Cinema 4D application/SDK and necessary plugins with supported deployment rights; real native runs required.

cards.title: CAD and BIM tessellation with retained metadata
cards.deliverable: Add specialist STEP/IGES and IFC adapters using qualified OCCT and IfcOpenShell builds. Tessellate supported surfaces/solids with configurable tolerances while retaining assemblies, units, object identifiers and useful BIM properties. Preserve construction sources and document semantics that runtime meshes cannot express.
cards.acceptance: Reference CAD assemblies and IFC buildings import at correct scale with selectable component identity and usable derived traversal. Changing tessellation tolerances creates new derivatives without changing originals. Export states precisely which metadata and geometry representations survive.
cards.tests: Compare bounds, tolerances, assembly transforms, IFC identifiers and property mappings against native references; test complex surfaces, absent units and unsupported entity types.
cards.security: Bound tessellation complexity, schema expansion and metadata payloads; isolate parsers and inventory actual dependency licenses.
external: Representative CAD/BIM source files and reference outputs; specialist binary builds must be qualified on deployment workers.

cards.title: Alembic and bounded simulation-cache playback
cards.deliverable: Implement an Alembic/cache adapter with explicit support for constant-topology deformation and a bounded changing-topology sequence route. Preserve source timing and dependency data; supply runtime playback and bundle serialization without mislabeling every cache as skeletal glTF. Define independent static or authored collision representations.
cards.acceptance: Qualified cache sequences play, seek, loop and restore after world export/reimport with their intended timing. Unsupported topology or storage requirements produce actionable results. Cache loading remains incremental and respects declared memory budgets.
cards.tests: Compare sampled vertices and frame timing with source references; exercise sparse frames, topology changes, seeking, interrupted loading, loop seams and bundle round trips.
cards.security: Enforce decompressed-frame, sequence-duration, memory and decoder-time budgets; isolate archive/cache parsers.
external: Representative native cache sequences and reference samples are needed to qualify each advertised cache feature.

cards.title: Point-cloud and Gaussian-splat streaming adapters
cards.deliverable: Implement specialized point-cloud and Gaussian-splat adapters with explicit schema detection, spatial streaming, picking and renderer integration. Preserve originals and component metadata; generate or attach separately qualified collision/traversal surfaces. Store adapter state and dependencies in world bundles and expose honest edit/export capabilities.
cards.acceptance: Representative scans stream at the selected device profile, retain scale and placement, and round-trip through complete world export. Visual splats are never treated automatically as solid meshes. Unsupported splat schemas are identified before placement.
cards.tests: Measure memory and frame timing, compare representative views, test point/splat classification, picking, cell transitions, collider alignment and bundle reconstruction.
cards.security: Bound point counts, attribute sizes and GPU allocations; validate custom attributes and isolate specialized decoding.
external: Selected renderer-adapter support and representative scan datasets must pass actual browser/device qualification.

cards.title: Complete asset coverage and representative venue acceptance
cards.deliverable: Publish the complete format/version/feature matrix and reproducible qualification corpus. Run the full intake, conversion, edit, optimization, physics and export workflow on substantial architecture and complex animated wildlife. Include direct-artist source/runtime deliverables, foreign-engine exchange exports, reference views and machine-readable results.
cards.acceptance: Every advertised native connector has passed real provisioned-toolchain conversion, and every format has meaningful feature and failure evidence. Venue openings, clips, materials and editable round trips pass; incomplete native dependencies remain visibly incomplete rather than credited to exchange workarounds.
cards.tests: Run corpus regression, cold/warm cache paths, corrupt dependencies, retry/cancel recovery and representative-device resource measurements against pinned builds.
cards.security: Perform malicious-import and cross-tenant export probes against the integrated pipeline and verify source preservation after failures.
external: Obtain representative source and runtime assets directly or by commission; native tools and required reference hardware must be available.

cards.title: Implement authenticated remote URL import and fetch brokerage
cards.deliverable: Implement authenticated remote-source submission and a tenant-scoped fetch broker. Identify formats, preserve retrieved originals and provenance, and hand successful downloads to the existing asset/media preparation pipeline. Support bounded streaming downloads, cancellation, retries and actionable failure states.
cards.acceptance: An authorized user imports a permitted remote model or media file through the same publication workflow as an upload. Invalid destinations, redirects or failed downloads cannot create a misleading published asset or expose internal services.
cards.tests: Run real permitted fetches plus private-address, DNS-change, redirect-chain, oversized-body, timeout and interrupted-transfer cases; verify source preservation, idempotency and cleanup.
cards.security: Authorize destination and tenant scope, revalidate DNS and every redirect, bind connections to validated addresses, restrict private/internal destinations and egress, strip unrelated credentials and enforce size/time limits.

cards.title: Define versioned world networking contracts and adapters
cards.deliverable: Publish application-neutral contracts for room joins, input commands, acknowledgments, snapshots, transient poses, simulation clocks and connection lifecycle. Define message versions, entity identifiers, sequence numbers, idempotency keys and compatibility negotiation. Implement the selected networking adapter behind those contracts, with local and deterministic fixture transports for development.
cards.acceptance: An engine client negotiates a compatible protocol, joins a fixture room and exchanges typed state without conference imports. Unsupported versions fail with an actionable upgrade result. Commands and disposable poses have distinct documented delivery requirements.
cards.tests: Exercise valid and malformed wire fixtures, version negotiation, duplicate commands, stale sequences and adapter teardown; retain compatibility fixtures for future releases.
cards.security: Bound decoded sizes and collection lengths before allocation. Treat client identifiers, timestamps and requested operations as untrusted input.

cards.title: Implement authenticated authoritative room membership
cards.deliverable: Implement Colyseus-backed room creation, join, leave and lifecycle APIs using the foundation choice. Bind each room to an immutable world revision and tenant. Exchange host-application authorization for short-lived engine grants, then maintain server-verified membership, capabilities, participant identity and connection status without embedding conference roles.
cards.acceptance: Two generic applications can join authorized worlds through the same API. Expired, revoked, wrong-instance and wrong-tenant grants fail. Rejoining retains the intended principal identity while duplicate active sessions follow an explicit policy.
cards.tests: Run multi-tenant integration cases covering grant renewal, disconnect, duplicate identity, incompatible world revision, denied join and clean room disposal.
cards.security: Recheck capabilities on protected operations; a successful join is not permission to edit, publish media or administer the room. Keep service credentials server-side.

cards.title: Run the world through a fixed-step authoritative simulation
cards.deliverable: Connect room lifecycle to the renderer-independent physics runtime and a bounded fixed-step input queue. Separate simulation frequency, publication rate and client rendering. Validate movement and interactions against authoritative collision, apply explicit limits to dynamic entities, and expose snapshots without writing every tick into persistent authoring history.
cards.acceptance: Multiple clients observe one authoritative object state, floor and wall layout. Client quality settings do not change collision. Unauthorized teleports, excessive command rates and attempts to create unbounded bodies are rejected predictably.
cards.tests: Run shared collision fixtures at configured tick rates; inject delayed inputs, overloaded ticks and invalid movement while measuring tick headroom and queue limits.
cards.security: Treat client transforms as requests. Validate magnitude, finite numbers, world bounds and capabilities before modifying the physics state.

cards.title: Add client prediction, reconciliation and remote interpolation
cards.deliverable: Integrate qualified Colyseus prediction and reconciliation primitives with the shared movement simulation. Buffer and acknowledge inputs, replay unacknowledged movement after authoritative corrections, and interpolate remote entity poses. Keep actual headset tracking local while reconciling the avatar body and validated locomotion; publish measurable correction and interpolation diagnostics.
cards.acceptance: Local movement responds immediately while server corrections converge. Remote avatars move smoothly through publication gaps. Crossing a wall cannot become permanent through prediction, and correction never forcibly replaces the headset's real tracked pose.
cards.tests: Exercise latency, jitter, reordered snapshots, reconnect and correction under the qualified browser/runtime versions; measure error without assuming cross-platform bitwise physics determinism.
cards.security: Server validation remains authoritative regardless of prediction. Bound retained input history, reconciliation work and accepted client clock skew.

cards.title: Arbitrate object interactions through expiring control leases
cards.deliverable: Implement a reusable server-owned lease primitive and apply it to grab, carry, release, throw and interaction commands. Bind leases to principal, entity, operation, expiry and authority epoch. Resolve simultaneous requests deterministically, validate ongoing movement, and emit interaction results that clients can predict and reconcile.
cards.acceptance: Only one authorized holder controls a contested object. Disconnect, expiry, deletion and authority changes release or invalidate ownership. An explicit save can later persist selected transforms; routine object movement does not modify the reusable world template.
cards.tests: Exercise competing grabs, stale holder commands, lease renewal races, disconnect while carrying, excessive throws and entity deletion during an interaction.
cards.security: Check capability, reach, allowed velocity and object constraints server-side. Never accept possession merely because the client renders an object as selected.

cards.title: Bound network traffic and protect reliable commands
cards.deliverable: Add separate outbound scheduling for acknowledged commands, essential state and replaceable poses. Begin with secure WebSockets: coalesce superseded poses before sending, bound all queues, apply backpressure and prioritize control traffic. Expose byte, queue-age and drop metrics; keep a transport extension point without claiming WebSocket frames are unreliable datagrams.
cards.acceptance: A slow client cannot accumulate unlimited memory. Release commands outrank unsent decorative updates; transport head-of-line delay remains measured. Queue overflow follows explicit degradation and reconnect rules, and pose publication can slow independently of simulation and rendering.
cards.tests: Throttle links, suspend receivers, flood decorative changes and resume traffic; verify memory bounds, command acknowledgments, coalescing and stale-update rejection.
cards.security: Enforce per-principal message and byte limits, bounded parsing and fair scheduling. Disconnect abusive senders without starving unrelated room members.

cards.title: Add spatial relevance and per-client state filtering
cards.deliverable: Maintain a spatial index and explicit relevance tiers for avatars, props and transient events. Use qualified Colyseus per-client filtering for bounded state sets, reduce distant pose detail and expose authorized proximity signals to media adapters. Send immutable assets through manifests and storage rather than frequent room patches.
cards.acceptance: Crossing a relevance boundary adds and removes entities without flicker or stale ghosts. Nearby interactions retain required fidelity, while distant traffic decreases. Private entities remain absent from unauthorized state even when geometrically close.
cards.tests: Move clients through dense cells, teleports and rapidly changing visibility; measure filtering CPU, serialization time, payload size and transition correctness with realistic avatar data.
cards.security: Intersect relevance with permissions before serialization. Distance and visibility are optimization inputs, never authorization. Bound per-client tracked sets and transition work.

cards.title: Route rooms to fenced owners across a worker fleet
cards.deliverable: Implement room placement, owner discovery and routing to the process that hosts each room. Add owner leases with monotonically changing epochs, admission based on measured capacity profiles, and drain-aware placement. Qualify the selected Redis-compatible coordination implementation, including Valkey only after testing the exact commands, scripts, TTLs and failover behavior used.
cards.acceptance: A join reaches its current owner behind a nonsticky load balancer. Fenced workers cannot commit as concurrent authorities. Adding workers increases room capacity without claiming that one room spans unlimited processes.
cards.tests: Exercise owner contention, expired leases, coordinator restart, TLS, script compatibility, network partitions and randomized reconnect routing in a multi-worker harness.
cards.security: Authenticate coordination and worker traffic; validate routing grants and epochs. Prevent clients from selecting an unauthorized internal worker or tenant.
external: A qualified coordination service with the required Redis protocol behavior and a deployment path that can route connections to room owners.

cards.title: Recover rooms through checkpoints and controlled reconnects
cards.deliverable: Persist versioned checkpoints of recoverable transient state, world revision references and command progress. Implement reconnect negotiation, checkpoint restoration, owner-epoch changes and planned drain handoff. Distinguish durable edits from recoverable motion and document potential checkpoint loss; use controlled reconnects until uninterrupted migration is actually demonstrated.
cards.acceptance: A crashed room restores to a declared checkpoint and clients converge on its new authority. Stale leases and duplicate commands cannot replay ownership or saved edits. Planned deployment drains stop new admissions and guide existing clients through recovery.
cards.tests: Kill workers during grabs and checkpoints, corrupt a snapshot, retry commands and roll service versions forward/back within the supported compatibility window.
cards.security: Reauthorize returning principals and validate checkpoint provenance. Do not restore expired credentials or persist unnecessary detailed head/hand tracking history.

cards.title: Provide authenticated Yjs collaboration and persistence
cards.deliverable: Create an application-neutral Yjs provider for notes, whiteboards and annotations with document-scoped authorization, persistence, bounded updates and ephemeral awareness. Separate document identity from room identity so explicitly permitted documents can survive sessions. Define an opaque encrypted-update transport extension without treating Yjs as the authority for physics or presenter control.
cards.acceptance: Concurrent edits converge after disconnect and reload. A document can be shared across authorized instances without leaking into another tenant. Read-only members cannot submit persisted changes, and transient cursor awareness does not become permanent tracking history.
cards.tests: Exercise concurrent edits, compaction/reload, reconnect, oversized updates, revocation, denied document IDs and persistence failure with recovery.
cards.security: Authorize every document subscription and write. Limit update size and processing cost; sanitize rendered content separately from CRDT convergence.

cards.title: Add scoped chat and ephemeral collaboration channels
cards.deliverable: Provide generic room, group and direct-participant message channels with server-assigned ordering, idempotent sends, pagination and configurable retention. Add bounded ephemeral channels for reactions, pointers and presence. Expose moderation capabilities and lifecycle events for applications without implementing event roles, agendas or a conference-specific moderation interface.
cards.acceptance: Authorized members can exchange messages across reconnects without duplicates. Membership changes stop future delivery, and ephemeral signals expire. Applications select retention and deletion policies through engine APIs rather than modifying the transport implementation.
cards.tests: Verify ordering, repeated sends, private group transitions, deletion, pagination, denied recipients, rate limiting and reconnect after missed traffic.
cards.security: Check channel membership on send and receive. Render untrusted text safely, bound attachments, and prevent user-controlled identifiers from crossing tenant boundaries.

cards.title: Qualify networking under realistic load and failure
cards.deliverable: Build repeatable multi-client and multi-room qualification scenarios with representative avatar poses, dynamic objects, interactions and collaborative edits. Exercise proposed 20, 50 and 100 participant profiles while measuring owner CPU, tick headroom, serialization, bandwidth, memory and recovery. Publish passing configurations and limits rather than a universal participant claim.
cards.acceptance: A standalone networking qualification harness works without conference services; W21 separately verifies the packaged game examples. Load and fault results identify the supported interaction profile, software versions and hardware. Rooms recover without split authority, unbounded queues or cross-tenant delivery.
cards.tests: Combine network impairment, worker/coordinator failures, rolling upgrades, competing grabs and document traffic; retain traces and reproducible fixture commands as release evidence.
cards.security: Include hostile message rates, forged grants and relevance-boundary access attempts. Use synthetic principals and exclude private content from diagnostic traces.
external: Representative load hosts and target network profiles sized to the proposed qualification scenarios.

cards.title: Coordinate revocation and generic moderation across services
cards.deliverable: Implement engine operations for removing principals, restricting publication/editing, expiring bans and invalidating control leases across world, media and collaboration services. Publish idempotent revocation events with measurable enforcement latency. Persist membership/revocation events and consumer acknowledgments. Apply them to collaboration writes/subscriptions, durable editing, presenter leases and device eligibility for future key envelopes; M16 consumes the same event lifecycle.
cards.acceptance: Removal stops protected activity and future media delivery across active connections and reconnects. Host applications define role policy while the engine enforces scoped actions; partial service failure has a documented fail-closed path.
cards.tests: Exercise revocation races, unavailable consumers, stale grants, repeat commands, ban expiry and attempts to retain an active presenter or grab lease. Verify one removal across world commands, documents, editing, presenter/grab leases, media admission and key-envelope eligibility.
cards.security: Authorize the moderator and target scope, retain safe audit records and prevent cross-tenant removal or silent access restoration after recovery.

cards.title: Implement durable world revisions and authoring transactions
cards.deliverable: Implement the server APIs for world templates, revisioned entity changes, idempotent command groups, history queries, optimistic conflicts and explicit snapshot publication. Keep these generic APIs independent of the browser editor and live physics ticks.
cards.acceptance: Two authorized clients can commit disjoint changes and receive explicit conflicts on incompatible edits. Undo creates a valid compensating revision. A published world references a consistent immutable dependency set.
cards.tests: Run database integration tests for concurrent commits, retries, interrupted transactions, migration, history visibility and snapshot restoration.
cards.security: Validate principal, tenant, entity and dependency read permissions; audit changes without recording transient participant tracking or embedding credentials in world data.

cards.title: Establish the shared spatial-audio graph and listener contract
cards.deliverable: Define serializable AudioEmitter and AudioZone components plus source adapters for buffers, media elements and live tracks. Build the Babylon AudioEngine v2/Web Audio integration with one local listener, category buses and explicit nonspatial modes. Bind listener position/orientation to desktop camera or XR head pose using canonical meters and coordinates.
cards.acceptance: A world source routes through exactly one spatial path. Entering or leaving XR switches the listener without duplicate audio or one listener per eye. World video defaults to spatial playback; global amplification requires an explicit configuration.
cards.tests: Verify coordinate fixtures, head rotation, camera changes, graph ownership, source disposal and serialization round trips using deterministic audio probes.
cards.security: Source references resolve through authorized engine assets or tracks. Do not allow imported scene data to execute arbitrary audio-processing scripts.

cards.title: Implement attached sounds, distance curves and continuous music mixing
cards.deliverable: Add reusable short-sound buffers, streaming loops and entity/local-offset attachments. Implement configured attenuation, reference distance, rolloff, directional cones and a separate fade-start/audible-radius envelope. Preserve explicit mono/stereo handling and support calibration metadata. Attach sources to interpolated transforms so animated birds and moving objects carry their sounds smoothly.
cards.acceptance: Four distinct calibrated corner tracks remain continuously mixed with equal attenuation at equal distance; approaching a corner changes the balance smoothly. A bird's source follows its transform. Inverse falloff still reaches zero at the engine's configured cutoff.
cards.tests: Measure gain and channel behavior with fixtures; exercise loops, changing distance, replacement, moving attachments and HRTF/equal-power profiles.
cards.security: Bound decoding and cached buffers by published asset limits. Reject nonfinite gains or malformed distance settings before constructing audio nodes.

cards.title: Add area emitters, acoustic zones and bounded occlusion
cards.deliverable: Implement authored point, line and area-source approximations for waterfalls and broad sound features. Add optional acoustic zones, bounded collision-query occlusion, smooth low-pass/gain changes and modest reverb sends. Publish editable parameters and serialization hooks while keeping all sources within one coherent gain and phase model.
cards.acceptance: A waterfall grows louder near its authored extent rather than only near its center. Crossing zone boundaries remains smooth. Multiple emitters do not accidentally multiply the source level, and geometric walls influence the configured approximation without claiming full acoustic simulation.
cards.tests: Check area edges, moving listener paths, zone overlaps, normalized multi-emitter output and query budgets; compare occluded and unobstructed fixtures.
cards.security: Acoustic attenuation never grants privacy. Bound emitter counts, impulse-response resources and per-frame geometry queries for creator-authored zones.

cards.title: Manage audio activation, mixing controls and resource budgets
cards.deliverable: Implement gesture-based audio unlock, suspension/resume handling and per-user voice, video, music, ambience and effects controls with master headroom. Budget active decoders and panners independently of graphics. Virtualize inaudible loops with hysteresis and preserved timeline, and expose a listener policy for applications using an accessible 2D view.
cards.acceptance: Join activation works within browser permissions. Headset sleep and tab suspension recover without duplicate nodes. Resource pressure preserves prioritized voice and presentations, while any quality downgrade retains distance behavior and avoids nearest-source switching among audible corner tracks.
cards.tests: Stress declared source budgets; cycle suspension, resume, scene reload and user mute; measure node/decoder cleanup and preserved loop positions.
cards.security: Enforce source limits even for trusted-looking manifests. Device and autoplay restrictions produce actionable state, never hidden attempts to bypass user permissions.

cards.title: Introduce the LiveKit media adapter behind engine contracts
cards.deliverable: Define media-session, publication, subscription and track-lifecycle interfaces independent of conference UI and world object semantics. Implement the selected LiveKit client/server adapter with stable source identities, connection state, mute/replacement events and service-side token issuance. Support both configured self-hosted and managed endpoints through the same public contract.
cards.acceptance: A generic engine sample publishes and receives media through the adapter without importing a meeting application. Switching endpoint configuration preserves object bindings. Reconnect and track replacement have explicit events that downstream spatial systems can consume.
cards.tests: Run adapter contract cases for join, publish, mute, replace, disconnect, reconnect and disposal; verify server/client version compatibility.
cards.security: Keep API secrets server-side. Bind issued media identities to verified engine principals and fail closed on unsupported or unauthorized publication requests.
external: A reachable LiveKit-compatible media service for integration testing; M07 supplies the self-hosted qualification environment.

cards.title: Enforce private media membership and subscription permissions
cards.deliverable: Map engine capabilities to narrow media-room, publication and subscription grants. Implement server-enforced private conversation membership, source permissions, renewal and revocation. Use separate authorized media rooms or verified server-side subscription enforcement where required; do not rely on client muting or a cooperative publisher to protect private streams. Implement a qualified self-hosted admission/revocation path at every signaling entry and reconnect, with membership epochs, no direct bypass and enforceable media-node checks for active-session access. Use a maintained server integration where needed; short token TTL alone is insufficient. Expiring authorization leases must bound active-session access when the control plane is unavailable.
cards.acceptance: A modified client cannot subscribe to an unauthorized nearby microphone, private group or tenant. Membership removal stops future delivery through the tested service path.
