Applications choose group policy while the engine enforces identities, scopes and operations. Original and server-refreshed cached tokens cannot restore removed permissions. Measure the maximum enforcement interval, including control-plane partitions, and keep the claim blocked until the configured enforcement mechanism passes.
cards.tests: Attempt direct SDK subscriptions, forged track IDs, reused grants, stale membership and cross-room access; test revocation during playback and reconnect. Reuse original/refreshed tokens after removal, attempt direct signaling access and interrupt management/control services during active media; verify bounded termination without granting stale access.
cards.security: Acoustic range and AOI are independent of permission. Document grant lifetime and revocation latency; never expose service administrator credentials to browsers.

cards.title: Ship a self-hosted SFU and TURN deployment harness
cards.deliverable: Provide pinned LiveKit and TURN configurations, local integration orchestration and a reference production deployment with explicit UDP/TCP ports, TLS, public addressing and health checks. Qualify coordination compatibility and node draining. Document the single-node room boundary, region placement and which hosting services can expose the required media networking.
cards.acceptance: Two external clients communicate through direct connectivity and forced TURN fallback. Multiple rooms distribute across the media fleet, while one room's capacity remains measured. Planned node drain and failure produce documented reconnect behavior and actionable diagnostics.
cards.tests: Exercise restricted networks, UDP blocking, TCP/TLS fallback, certificate renewal, coordinator interruption and media-node restart using external probes.
cards.security: Use authenticated expiring TURN credentials, restricted administration and secrets injection. Prevent the relay from becoming an unauthenticated public service. Expose signaling only through the qualified admission path and deploy the M06 media-node revocation/lease enforcement configuration.
external: UDP-capable test hosts with routable public addresses, DNS/TLS certificates and controlled external clients; generic HTTP-only hosting is insufficient.

cards.title: Attach remote microphones to avatars without duplicate playback
cards.deliverable: Wrap each selected incoming microphone track in a single-track media-stream audio source and bind it to the avatar's interpolated head/mouth offset. Reconcile track identity, mute, replacement and teardown with the media adapter. Publish local microphone capture outbound without default local monitoring or a simultaneous global conference audio renderer.
cards.acceptance: Walking avatars carry their voices; listener motion and head rotation change the mix appropriately. Muting, reconnecting or replacing a microphone never creates two playback paths. Missing avatars use an explicit temporary binding policy rather than silently becoming global audio.
cards.tests: Use two moving clients to check spatial gain, track replacement, mute, late avatar arrival, device permission denial and clean disposal.
cards.security: Create nodes only for authorized subscribed tracks. Revocation tears down playback promptly; local capture starts only after the browser's permission flow.

cards.title: Create generic media surfaces and an extensible viewer registry
cards.deliverable: Implement media-surface entities with source revision, aspect ratio, audio binding, preview state and disposal lifecycle. Add a registry for authorized viewers/converters and an attachment fallback that preserves originals. Expose the same content through world surfaces and accessible 2D views without assuming arbitrary websites, native applications or file formats render inside VR. Resolve imported external file sources through the A25 broker and preserve their publication identity.
cards.acceptance: Images, registered content and unknown attachments can be placed, replaced, moved and deleted without orphaned resources. Unsupported files receive a clear attachment/preview result. A surface exports and reimports with stable source and audio references.
cards.tests: Exercise registry selection, unsupported types, missing revisions, loading failures, replacement, lifecycle cleanup and serialization.
cards.security: Treat viewer plugins as trusted engine extensions. Resolve files through authorized storage and validate external fetches; never execute embedded active content automatically.

cards.title: Publish camera and screen capture onto world surfaces
cards.deliverable: Add explicit camera and desktop screen-capture workflows, publication controls and live textures. Associate captured audio with the intended screen/camera emitter without duplicating microphone playback. Provide a short-lived paired-device presentation capability so a desktop can originate a stream while a headset receives it; keep application presenter policy outside the engine.
cards.acceptance: A desktop user chooses the capture source through the browser prompt. Headsets display supported incoming streams regardless of their ability to originate capture. Stop-sharing, source termination and replacement update both picture and spatial sound.
cards.tests: Qualify capture denial, window/tab/system-audio variations, ended tracks, paired-device expiry and mixed microphone/screen audio on supported browsers.
cards.security: Require user activation and scoped publication grants. Pairing must bind verified principals and require explicit device confirmation; never silently capture another device.
external: Actual supported desktop browsers and headset receivers; available capture-audio sources vary by browser and operating system.

cards.title: Play uploaded video through one synchronized visual/audio element
cards.deliverable: Load qualified uploaded-video variants into one media element used by both the video texture and MediaElementAudioSourceNode. Connect its audio once to the screen emitter, expose play/pause/seek/loop controls and preserve source clock ownership. Handle authorized CDN access, CORS, codec selection and clear failure states.
cards.acceptance: A looping wall video sounds as if it comes from its screen, including after movement or replacement. Pausing and seeking affect picture and sound together. Muting its emitter removes that video's audio completely, with no independent global route.
cards.tests: Exercise loops, seeks, resize, disposal, unsupported codecs, expired URLs and CORS failures while measuring audio/video alignment.
cards.security: Use published validated variants and authorized delivery. Reject arbitrary decoder inputs beyond resource limits and avoid exposing signed media URLs in logs.

cards.title: Synchronize presentation control and media playback across clients
cards.deliverable: Apply server-owned presentation leases to source selection, page changes and video controls. Synchronize asset revision, source identity, sequence number, play state, position, rate and server-time anchor. Implement late-join reconstruction and measured drift correction; keep transient pointers separate from durable content and application-specific presenter selection. Register checkpoint/restore hooks for source revision, page, playback time anchor and controller epoch with N09; invalidate stale presenter leases after authority-owner changes.
cards.acceptance: Only the current authorized controller changes a surface. Late joiners reach the current page or video position, and lease expiry or handoff cannot replay stale controls. Each client shares playback state while retaining its own spatial audio mix.
cards.tests: Inject clock offset, delayed controls, duplicate seeks, simultaneous handoff, late join and buffering; measure drift and sequence convergence. Crash the world owner during active video and presenter handoff, restore the checkpoint and verify late-join reconstruction with a new authority epoch.
cards.security: Validate every control operation against entity scope and lease epoch. Source changes must reference authorized published content, not unchecked external URLs.

cards.title: Allocate media subscriptions from world visibility and audio relevance
cards.deliverable: Drive stream subscription and quality from projected surface size, visibility, priority and decoder budgets rather than hidden HTML-element dimensions alone. Add authorized voice pre-subscription margins, smooth fades and hysteresis around audible boundaries. Prioritize active presentations and speech while exposing policy hooks for applications and device profiles.
cards.acceptance: A visible video texture does not stop because its backing element is hidden. Crossing a voice range avoids rapid subscription churn and clipped initial speech under the qualified margin. Revoked streams are removed regardless of retention margins or priority.
cards.tests: Exercise occluded screens, moving listeners, rapid viewport changes, constrained decoder counts, competing streams and permission changes while measuring quality transitions.
cards.security: Intersect every optimization decision with server authorization. Client proximity requests cannot widen private media membership or bypass source permissions.

cards.title: Render PDF slides, images and readable text surfaces
cards.deliverable: Integrate PDF.js page rendering, image panels and text surfaces with bounded resolution, lazy page loading and accessible 2D text/navigation. Consume immutable office-to-PDF outputs and publish page metadata to presentation synchronization. Preserve original documents and show conversion limitations, including unsupported animations, fonts or embedded applications.
cards.acceptance: A presenter changes a slide once and authorized clients display the same page revision in desktop and immersive views. Nearby text remains readable within the qualified device budget. Users can access original files and choose screen sharing when static conversion loses essential behavior.
cards.tests: Use large-page, font, rotation, image and malformed-document fixtures; verify page identity, accessibility, resource limits and late joins.
cards.security: Disable automatic execution or navigation from document actions. Resolve external references through approved policies and isolate conversion outside the browser runtime.
external: The qualified office-conversion and font environment supplied by the document-conversion lane.

cards.title: Connect shared notes, whiteboards and page annotations to surfaces
cards.deliverable: Bind Yjs documents to reusable notes, whiteboard and annotation surfaces. Implement desktop and qualified XR input, vector strokes, selection and accessible editing views. Anchor annotations to asset revision and page coordinates; send pointers through ephemeral channels while preserving persistent content separately from server-owned presentation control.
cards.acceptance: Concurrent notes and strokes converge after reconnect. Page changes keep annotations on their correct page and source revision. Read-only viewers can follow presentations without acquiring edit authority, and world export retains permitted document references and content snapshots.
cards.tests: Exercise simultaneous edits, page switching, source replacement, disconnected drawing, permission changes, export/reimport and keyboard operation.
cards.security: Enforce document and surface permissions independently. Bound stroke density and text size, sanitize displayed content and prevent annotations from becoming executable scene behavior.

cards.title: Implement authenticated media E2EE keys and membership epochs
cards.deliverable: Define the E2EE threat model and implement a reviewed endpoint-authentication and key-envelope protocol around LiveKit's encryption support. Generate session epoch keys at authorized endpoints, distribute encrypted envelopes to verified devices, and rotate on membership changes. Handle late joins, reconnects, key loss, revocation and explicit recovery policy without plaintext keys in service logs. Consume N13 membership/revocation events for device eligibility and key-epoch changes. Scope keys to each actual authorized private media audience rather than sharing one world-wide key.
cards.acceptance: Only admitted endpoints obtain current media keys. Removed devices cannot decrypt future epochs; key loss fails visibly rather than silently disabling encryption. Document that signaling metadata remains server-visible and that revocation cannot erase previously received content.
cards.tests: Exercise device substitution, forged envelopes, late join, removal, reconnect, rotation races and unsupported-browser failure using reviewed protocol fixtures.
cards.security: Use established cryptographic primitives and authenticated endpoint identities. Block production E2EE claims until protocol and integration review passes.
external: A reviewed browser-compatible key-envelope/group-key implementation and security review of endpoint authentication and key lifecycle.

cards.title: Protect shared content with explicit encrypted-processing boundaries
cards.deliverable: Add client-encrypted document updates, snapshots and prepared media/assets using the established key lifecycle and opaque storage/relay contracts. Keep server-required simulation state outside this promise. Provide explicit modes for local preparation or an admitted converter that can read source content; encrypted storage must not silently bypass validation or claim invisible server conversion.
cards.acceptance: Authorized clients restore encrypted shared documents and render prepared content after reconnect while storage contains ciphertext. Revoked members cannot obtain new epochs. Choosing server conversion or processing identifies the endpoint's access rather than describing it as outside the trust boundary.
cards.tests: Verify encrypted persistence/reload, tampering, wrong keys, large updates, key rotation and conversion-mode transitions with synthetic content.
cards.security: Authenticate ciphertext metadata and scope keys to content audiences. Keep client resource limits, provenance and access controls after decryption.

cards.title: Record sessions through an explicitly authorized processing endpoint
cards.deliverable: Provide recording start/stop/status APIs and a separate recording worker using qualified LiveKit egress or an admitted receiver endpoint. Define captured tracks, surface composition and synchronization metadata. Publish immutable recording artifacts with access and retention hooks. For encrypted sessions, admit a recorder with keys only through explicit application-approved processing policy. Implement a reusable program-composition input contract for live tracks, file-backed audio/video with M12 playback anchors and PDF/slide state. Select a produced mix or a defined listener/viewpoint mix; file-backed sources require content authorization and keys independently of media-track encryption.
cards.acceptance: Recording captures the declared program and produces playable, synchronized output with recoverable failure status. Private sessions cannot gain an undisclosed recorder. The API distinguishes ordinary egress from an E2EE-capable processing path instead of assuming stock egress decrypts arbitrary sessions. A live microphone, a PDF slide change and an uploaded wall video with soundtrack appear once each when selected, at the correct program times; excluded/private sources remain absent.
cards.tests: Exercise start/stop races, worker crash, missing tracks, key rotation, revoked recorder, retry idempotency and artifact deletion. Exercise the mixed live-track, slide and file-video fixture through capture and playback, checking source selection, timing, audio duplication and separate content/media key access.
cards.security: Authorize recording separately from listening. Scope processor keys and storage access, and avoid logging decrypted media or reusable credentials.
external: A deployed recording/egress worker with measured CPU capacity and durable artifact storage.

cards.title: Integrate authorized captions and transcription providers
cards.deliverable: Define a transcription provider contract and an explicitly admitted caption-processing endpoint. Route authorized audio, emit speaker/source identifiers and timestamped partial/final captions, and render readable captions in desktop, 2D and qualified XR surfaces. Expose transcript export, access and retention hooks while keeping application language and recording policy separate. Consume the M18 program-input contract, including selected file-backed audio; possession of media-track keys does not grant document or file access.
cards.acceptance: Captions track the selected audio program and remain aligned through source changes. Encrypted sessions identify the processor as a key-holding endpoint or disable processing clearly. Users can distinguish partial corrections and unavailable transcription from finalized text.
cards.tests: Use known speech fixtures, interruption, mixed sources, caption revisions, provider failure and key revocation; measure latency and documented recognition limits.
cards.security: Grant only necessary tracks and keys. Protect transcript artifacts as content, with tenant-scoped access and configurable deletion.
external: A selected and licensed self-hosted speech-recognition runtime/model or configured transcription provider, plus representative language fixtures.

cards.title: Relay a shared stage program across independent audience rooms
cards.deliverable: Implement a generic stage-program source with a common clock, track/source identifiers and an actual authorized relay or republishing worker into independent audience media rooms. Propagate presentation state with measured relay delay, reconnect and source replacement behavior. Keep audience world instances separate and expose topology controls for applications. Reuse the M18 program-input contract to coordinate live tracks, authorized file-backed video/audio timelines and slide state across audience rooms.
cards.acceptance: Clients in different audience rooms receive the same live program through real media delivery, not merely matching identifiers. One audience-room failure does not stop the stage. Capacity evidence separates stage publishers, relay fanout, per-room limits and aggregate attendance.
cards.tests: Exercise multiple rooms, relay interruption, publisher replacement, clock alignment, room churn and encrypted-mode key rotation under measured traffic.
cards.security: Authorize each relay destination and its source access. Any relay that decrypts content is an admitted processing endpoint, with explicit keys and trust.
external: Relay/republishing capacity and multi-room SFU infrastructure with routable media connectivity for load qualification.

cards.title: Deliver a produced broadcast with viewer-latency awareness
cards.deliverable: Add a produced-program broadcast adapter with qualified segmented video delivery, authenticated manifests and CDN/object-storage configuration. Map viewer playback time to the stage program clock so slides, annotations and application interactions can account for broadcast delay. Support lightweight and world-surface receivers, with spatial screen audio unless explicit amplification is selected.
cards.acceptance: Many receiver instances share a program without joining one unbounded interactive room. Late joins and buffering preserve the declared synchronization model. The API exposes latency and live-edge status rather than presenting delayed viewers as identical to stage participants.
cards.tests: Exercise buffering, seeking within the allowed window, token expiry, source discontinuity, CDN failure and viewer-time alignment. Verify the microphone, changing PDF and uploaded wall-video soundtrack fixture end to end, with each chosen input captured once and private inputs excluded.
cards.security: Protect manifests and segments with scoped access. Document revocation/cache/buffer limits; broadcast distribution does not automatically preserve media E2EE.
external: A selected broadcast packaging path and CDN/object store supporting required access controls, media formats and CORS.

cards.title: Promote audience participants into live publishing safely
cards.deliverable: Implement application-neutral promotion and demotion transactions between audience reception and authorized live publishing. Obtain fresh grants, establish the interactive connection, transfer relevant control leases and switch playback paths with feedback prevention. Provide status and rollback hooks; applications decide who is invited, accepted or returned to the audience.
cards.acceptance: An authorized audience member can join the live stage without hearing a delayed copy of themselves or retaining duplicate program audio. Failed promotion returns to a usable audience state. Demotion revokes publication and restores the appropriate audience clock and subscriptions.
cards.tests: Exercise accepted/declined invitations, slow permissions, reconnect mid-transition, duplicate requests, source-device failure and simultaneous handoffs.
cards.security: Reauthorize at each boundary, expire transfer grants and revoke old capabilities. Audience membership alone cannot acquire microphone or presenter authority.

cards.title: Qualify the complete spatial-media graph on real devices
cards.deliverable: Run reproducible end-to-end scenarios combining four-corner music, moving birds, avatar microphones, area waterfalls, looping screens and live presentations. Qualify laptop speakers, headphones and actual headsets through the final graph, including echo cancellation, output-device changes and resume. Publish supported browser/device configurations, source budgets, drift, frame/audio cost and network conditions.
cards.acceptance: Spatial behavior, permission enforcement and single-route playback survive reconnect and source replacement. Acoustic quality remains usable under the declared concurrent load. Stage, broadcast, recording and caption results identify their different latency, trust and capacity profiles.
cards.tests: Include blind listening checks, instrumented gain fixtures, restricted-network runs, device swaps, processor failure and hostile subscription attempts; retain evidence for release.
cards.security: Use consented test participants and synthetic content. Verify no private tracks, plaintext keys or transcript content enter diagnostics.
external: Reference laptops with speakers/headphones, actual supported headsets, external network probes and consented human listeners for perceptual and echo tests.

cards.title: Implement video and audio preparation workers
cards.deliverable: Integrate pinned FFmpeg workers for metadata probing, browser-playable video/audio variants, thumbnails and loudness metadata. Define supported codec/container profiles, preserve originals and publish immutable derived media through the asset pipeline.
cards.acceptance: Representative uploaded media plays through the supported browser profiles with the correct duration, channel layout and seek behavior. Invalid input and unavailable codecs produce clear diagnostics rather than silent audio loss.
cards.tests: Test variable frame rate, silent and multi-channel inputs, corrupt containers, large files, cancellation, retry and resulting browser playback.
cards.security: Run untrusted containers under resource/egress limits, audit the actual FFmpeg build and prevent path, playlist or remote-reference escape.

cards.title: Implement office document conversion and safe previews
cards.deliverable: Integrate a pinned headless office converter for supported presentation/document inputs, PDF/page outputs and thumbnails. Package fonts and record conversion differences; expose original retrieval and desktop sharing for features that static pages cannot preserve.
cards.acceptance: Representative slide decks and documents yield readable page sequences with correct order and useful font/layout diagnostics. Encrypted, corrupt or unsupported inputs have explicit outcomes; embedded macros do not execute.
cards.tests: Compare reference pages, fonts, images, slide order, failures and cancellation; verify output through the browser PDF renderer when M14 is integrated.
cards.security: Isolate office parsing, disable active content and network references, enforce file/page/resource limits and retain private-document access controls.

cards.title: Qualify core spatial audio and laptop echo behavior
cards.deliverable: Run the core four-corner, moving-source, waterfall and wall-video audio scenarios on headphones, laptop speakers and actual supported headsets. Exercise microphone echo cancellation through the final playback graph and record core source/decoder budgets.
cards.acceptance: Equally calibrated sources have matching distance gains at equal distances; movement changes the mix continuously. Video audio remains screen-attached with one route. Simultaneous conversation and video remain usable without feedback under the declared profile.
cards.tests: Measure gain/cutoff behavior and A/V drift; perform listening, device-change, reconnect, permission-denial and headset-resume checks with real output/capture devices.
cards.security: Confirm private streams stay inaccessible and diagnostic output contains no audio content or keys; failures remain release blockers for affected profiles.
external: Reference laptop speakers/headphones and actual supported headsets

cards.title: Adapt the browser editor shell and scene selection
cards.deliverable: Wrap the qualified browser authoring foundation or build missing shell components: hierarchy outline, viewport selection, inspector hosting, tool modes and host-injected authorization. Keep editor packages application-neutral and reusable independently of conference administration.
cards.acceptance: An imported world exposes stable selectable entities and hierarchy without duplicating renderer-owned objects. Selection stays synchronized between outline and viewport. Keyboard navigation, focus transitions and read-only mode work, and replacing the world clears obsolete selections safely.
cards.tests: Exercise nested/instanced scenes, multi-selection, deleted entities, keyboard operation and scene replacement in browser tests; inspect accessible names and focus order.
cards.security: Read-only presentation is not enforcement; editor commands require a valid capability and sanitize asset-provided labels before display.

cards.title: Add transactional transforms, cloning and prefab editing
cards.deliverable: Implement transform gizmos, numeric entry, snapping, reparenting, cloning and prefab instance overrides through a shared authoring-command model. Provide local preview and reversible grouped edits while preserving source pivots and stable object identity.
cards.acceptance: Dragging a group creates one logical undo step rather than a history entry per frame. Cloning allocates new identifiers, prefab overrides remain distinct from source definitions and reparenting preserves intended world transforms. Cancelled gestures restore the original scene.
cards.tests: Cover rotated parents, negative scales, group transforms, prefab overrides, cancel/undo/redo and invalid parent cycles against independent fixtures.
cards.security: Validate numeric bounds and entity scopes before committing commands; previews cannot bypass protected-object capabilities.

cards.title: Expose material, lighting and environment authoring
cards.deliverable: Add inspectors for supported physically based material properties, texture assignment, lights, shadows, sky, water and weather settings. Reuse selected renderer editors where compatible and store changes as portable component data or declared renderer extensions.
cards.acceptance: Users edit a material instance without unexpectedly changing unrelated shared materials. Light and environment changes preview correctly, undo cleanly and survive serialization. Unsupported shader features remain visible as preserved metadata with explicit limitations rather than silently resetting.
cards.tests: Exercise shared-versus-instance edits, texture replacement, renderer-extension preservation, undo and low-quality preview behavior with reference materials.
cards.security: Permit only validated asset references and bounded rendering parameters; arbitrary shader or node input follows the trusted-extension policy.

cards.title: Deliver drag-and-drop import, catalog and placement flows
cards.deliverable: Connect files, folders and archives to resumable imports, job progress, diagnostics and the reusable asset catalog/inventory. Support quick runtime-asset placement, delayed conversion placeholders and source retrieval without vendor-specific controls or conference-only workflows.
cards.acceptance: Dropping a supported asset leads to an editable placed object or an actionable conversion result. Retries do not duplicate published assets or placements. Cancelled jobs and missing textures remain understandable, and users can reuse an existing asset without reuploading it.
cards.tests: Exercise ready GLB, archive dependencies, interrupted upload, retry, cancellation, failed conversion and placement after asynchronous completion.
cards.security: Enforce upload/catalog/placement capabilities and tenant boundaries; display converter diagnostics safely and retain server resource limits.

cards.title: Provide collision, navigation and spawn authoring tools
cards.deliverable: Add overlays and editing controls for collider assignments, simplified shapes, collision groups, navigation tiles, teleport regions, portals and spawn locations. Expose rebuild status and diagnostics while preserving the separation between visual geometry and physical representation.
cards.acceptance: A host can inspect blocked doorways, repair a collider or spawn point, rebuild affected navigation and validate traversal. Pending rebuilds cannot publish a falsely ready walkable area. Edits have clear undo behavior and preserve unchanged regions.
cards.tests: Use venue fixtures with arches, stairs and deliberately broken colliders; verify rebuild cancellation, stale result rejection and safe-spawn validation.
cards.security: Authorize physics edits separately from ordinary placement; reject malicious shape parameters and dangerous spawn destinations.

cards.title: Implement browser terrain sculpting and tile updates
cards.deliverable: Add bounded terrain sculpt/flatten/smooth and surface-paint tools with brush preview, grouped stroke transactions and tiled dirty-region updates. Coordinate visual, collider and navigation revisions so live editing cannot produce silent disagreement between rendered and physical terrain.
cards.acceptance: A stroke crossing tile borders preserves seams and undoes as one operation. Rebuild progress and temporarily unavailable regions are visible. Removing a supporting surface triggers the established participant recovery policy before publication, and unchanged tiles retain their identities.
cards.tests: Exercise border strokes, large undo operations, interrupted rebuilds, negative elevations, concurrent invalidation and world reload after terrain edits.
cards.security: Limit brush extent, changed-tile counts and rebuild frequency; enforce terrain-edit capabilities independently of object manipulation.

cards.title: Author media surfaces, sound emitters and acoustic zones
cards.deliverable: Provide reusable inspectors for screen geometry, source bindings, playback policy, emitter attachments, distance curves, directional cones, mixer buses and acoustic zones. Add visual falloff/zone overlays and a listener preview using existing media/audio systems.
cards.acceptance: Users place a wall video with one spatial soundtrack, attach sound to an animal and configure overlapping corner tracks. Moving or duplicating objects preserves intended bindings without accidental duplicate playback. Acoustic changes undo and reload; private-media authorization remains distinct from audible radius.
cards.tests: Verify save/reload of media/audio settings, duplicate-binding prevention, emitter offsets, overlapping ranges and acoustic-zone editing.
cards.security: Validate source access and playback-control grants; authoring an audible zone cannot grant access to a private conversation.

cards.title: Author behavior graphs, actor settings and attachments
cards.deliverable: Expose declarative trigger/action editing, clip selection, NPC route configuration, attachment sockets and component diagnostics through reusable editor panels. Reuse qualified graph tools; the core editor supports declared behaviors while general creator-code editing follows the isolated-runtime expansion.
cards.acceptance: An author configures a door trigger, animated route and wearable attachment without editing source files. References survive cloning and prefab overrides. Invalid action graphs, missing clips and broken sockets prevent misleading publication and remain repairable after reload.
cards.tests: Exercise behavior graph validation, component-reference remapping, route previews, clip changes, attachment replacement and undo across actor edits.
cards.security: Editor previews execute only approved actions in a constrained context; privileged runtime effects require normal authority checks.

cards.title: Persist collaborative edits, revision history and undo
cards.deliverable: Connect authoring commands to durable revisions, idempotent commits, edit leases or optimistic version checks and collaborative change notifications. Add revision history, conflict resolution and reversible command groups without using a document CRDT as physics authority.
cards.acceptance: Two editors changing the same entity receive a consistent commit or explicit conflict. Disjoint permitted changes persist, retries create no duplicate revisions and revocation stops further commits. Undo respects intervening edits instead of restoring a stale whole-world snapshot.
cards.tests: Run concurrent browser editors against persistence with dropped acknowledgments, stale revisions, expired leases, retries, reconnect and conflicting undo.
cards.security: Validate actor, tenant, expected revision and entity scopes server-side; history must not expose inaccessible assets or other tenants' edits.

cards.title: Complete world export, reimport and live-to-template saves
cards.deliverable: Connect browser workflows to complete world-bundle export/reimport, supported GLB export, original retrieval and explicit capture of selected live changes into a new template revision. Reuse asset-lane exporters and surface fidelity/loss reports instead of duplicating conversion code.
cards.acceptance: A world round-trip preserves IDs, prefab overrides, terrain, collisions, behaviors, media and source references. Saving thrown-object placements creates an intentional new revision without recording physics ticks. GLB limitations are explicit, and export never silently removes supported editing capabilities.
cards.tests: Round-trip a composite authored world, compare semantic manifests, restore captured runtime placements and test missing dependencies, migration and interrupted exports.
cards.security: Check export/read capabilities per dependency and exclude live credentials, participant records, private keys and ephemeral tracking from bundles.

cards.title: Package the reproducible local and hosted service stack
cards.deliverable: Provide local composition and deployable infrastructure for control API, world fleet, media/TURN, collaboration, queue, database and storage. Separate HTTP/WebSocket routing from UDP-capable media infrastructure and document capacity assumptions.
cards.acceptance: A fresh environment can launch the selected stack and run a two-client room with asset processing and live media. No service silently depends on a developer workstation or hosted editor account.
cards.tests: Run clean provisioning, service discovery, health/readiness, dependency outage and teardown/recreate tests.
cards.security: Use scoped identities, private service paths, secret references and minimal exposed ports. Keep local convenience settings out of production defaults.
external: Selected hosting resources exposing required HTTP/WebSocket and media transports

cards.title: Harden transport secrets keys and service boundaries
cards.deliverable: Complete environment-specific TLS, secure WebSockets, TURN credentials, service authentication, key rotation, secret distribution and browser policy configuration. Document data classes, retention and server-visible processing boundaries.
cards.acceptance: Expired credentials fail closed, rotation works without cross-tenant access, and supported encrypted modes match their stated participants and processors. Browser bundles contain no service secrets. Session revocation follows the measured M06 enforcement path; a JWT expiry timestamp is not treated as active-session termination.
cards.tests: Test token/key expiry, rotation, downgraded transport, origin/cross-site abuse and key-loss recovery according to the documented policy.
cards.security: Apply the standing end-to-end security standard to each actual data flow; do not claim certification or hide necessary trusted endpoints.

cards.title: Add metrics tracing capacity budgets and cost controls
cards.deliverable: Instrument frame time, asset latency, conversion time, world tick, queue depth, room placement, subscriptions, decoder/audio load and recovery. Add budget alerts and safe diagnostic export using opaque session IDs.
cards.acceptance: Operators can distinguish client rendering, simulation, media and network bottlenecks, and can account for per-event participant minutes, bandwidth and worker consumption.
cards.tests: Inject representative failures/load and verify correlation, alert delivery, metric bounds and log redaction.
cards.security: Exclude private document/media content and raw tracking streams; restrict diagnostics and prevent user-controlled labels from exhausting monitoring resources.

cards.title: Qualify persistence migration backups and restoration
cards.deliverable: Implement backup/restore procedures for metadata, world revisions, collaboration documents and asset manifests, with explicit retention and recovery targets. Use compatible migrations and rehearsed restore or forward-repair plans.
cards.acceptance: A clean environment can restore an internally consistent world and its assets at a documented recovery point. Retried restores do not duplicate jobs or revive revoked grants unintentionally.
cards.tests: Run real database/object-storage restore, missing-asset detection, schema upgrade/downgrade compatibility and interrupted migration drills.
cards.security: Encrypt protected backups, restrict restore access, verify deletion/retention behavior and document key recovery separately from data recovery.

cards.title: Qualify restricted networks and service failure recovery
cards.deliverable: Exercise TURN fallback, bandwidth/latency/loss changes, WebSocket reconnect, worker drain/crash, media-node loss, converter restart and staged release rollback. Publish expected user-visible recovery and limitations.
cards.acceptance: Authorized clients recover predictably without duplicate room authorities, presenters or audio paths. Unsupported seamless migration is not advertised as achieved.
cards.tests: Run controlled fault scenarios through actual ingress and media paths; verify queue replay, lease epochs and checkpoint restoration. Repeat recovery with removed members holding original and refreshed media tokens, including unavailable control-plane services.
cards.security: Ensure recovery never drops authorization checks, restores stale media access or exposes abandoned temporary processing files.

cards.title: Qualify rendering audio and conference capacity profiles
cards.deliverable: Run reproducible desktop and real-headset workloads with architectural assets, animated wildlife, physics, four music sources, avatar voice and video screens. Test 20/50/100 interactive participants and concurrent interactive-room growth separately; R13 qualifies the expanded stage/broadcast topology.
cards.acceptance: Publish passing hardware/browser/workload profiles with p95/p99 frame timing, selected headset refresh, join latency, media quality, memory and service headroom. Failing configurations remain unsupported rather than receiving an invented capacity claim.
cards.tests: Use real media publishers/decoders plus load clients, repeat steady-state and burst joins, and retain raw measurements and configuration hashes.
cards.security: Verify load controls resist resource exhaustion and test with privacy modes enabled rather than disabling safeguards for better numbers.
external: Representative ordinary laptop, premium desktop and actual target headsets

cards.title: Complete integrated security and abuse verification
cards.deliverable: Execute the engine threat-model scenarios across tenant isolation, grants, uploads, converters, behaviors, media subscriptions, exports and administration. Add regression coverage for findings and record a separate self security review.
cards.acceptance: Blocking findings are fixed and verified on the candidate commit. A self-review is identified honestly; actual repository-required independent reviews remain enforced if configured.
cards.tests: Run cross-tenant and stale-token attacks, parser/sandbox escape fixtures, quotas, SSRF/path traversal, permission races and secret scans in deployed configurations.
cards.security: Do not weaken required checks or encryption to close the milestone. Record residual limitations with bounded impact and a concrete disposition.

cards.title: Qualify browser headset and accessible engine behavior
cards.deliverable: Define the supported browser/headset matrix and run input, locomotion, media, listener pose, readable surfaces, focus, permission-denial, sleep/resume and context-loss scenarios. Qualify optional hands/layers/trackers separately.
cards.acceptance: Each advertised combination has actual evidence and useful fallback behavior. The local accessibility example works without requiring immersive 3D navigation.
cards.tests: Run browser automation plus hands-on headset, keyboard/screen-reader and output-device scripts; preserve device/browser versions with results.
cards.security: Verify capture consent, safe focus transitions and privacy-consistent alternate views; do not use an emulator as sole hardware evidence.
external: Actual devices for every advertised immersive support profile

cards.title: Publish the engine beta with verified core contracts
cards.deliverable: Produce versioned SDK packages and service images with migration notes, immutable provenance and a compatibility matrix. Publish only the core functionality already exercised through the release checks, keeping expanded capabilities visibly pending.
cards.acceptance: A clean independent consumer can install the beta and run local and multiplayer examples. Released artifacts correspond to the tested commit and exclude unverified adapter claims.
cards.tests: Run package-consumer, API/schema compatibility, artifact integrity and upgrade/rollback smoke checks against released builds.
cards.security: Complete the core subset of R07 threat-model checks and a separate beta security review; no unresolved blocking finding may enter the beta.

cards.title: Complete SDK documentation integration examples and handoff
cards.deliverable: Publish getting-started guides, SDK/API references, plugin/converter authoring, world schemas, media/audio examples, deployment/runbooks and upgrade guidance. Maintain exact progress, dependency and evidence records for future agents and project dashboards.
cards.acceptance: A fresh developer can build a non-conference application, import/export a world and deploy a test room using repository instructions alone. Handoff includes unresolved external dependencies and the next runnable cards.
cards.tests: Execute documented commands and example projects in clean environments; validate links, schema examples and status/evidence references.
cards.security: Keep credentials out of documentation and examples, state privacy boundaries accurately and verify deployment examples use secure defaults.

cards.title: Qualify expanded formats and the requested reference assets
cards.deliverable: Run real native-tool connectors and the agreed architecture/animal corpus through conversion, editing, rendering tiers, collision/navigation and export. Record exact file/tool versions, approximation reports and supported feature subsets.
cards.acceptance: Every advertised native or specialist adapter has a real passing fixture; the Acropolis/eagle/futuristic-building scenarios have visual and functional evidence using actual supplied files. Exchange substitutes do not mark native loaders complete.
cards.tests: Compare reference renders/animations, traverse openings, place and throw props, inspect acoustic attachments and round-trip the complete edited world.
cards.security: Exercise malformed files and embedded code through isolated workers; preserve source access controls and immutable conversion provenance.
external: Actual reference models and provisioned native SDK/application/plugin environments

cards.title: Accept and release the complete general engine
cards.deliverable: Reconcile all core and expanded engine cards, publish supported capability/format/device profiles and produce the final versioned SDK and service release. Keep every reusable mechanism free of conference-specific runtime dependencies.
cards.acceptance: Every core and expanded engine card is implemented and verified against its required evidence. Any incomplete mandatory capability, unresolved blocking finding or missing required hardware, provider, asset or native-tool evidence blocks the complete release. A fresh host runs the general examples and deployment successfully.
cards.tests: Run the final package, migration, world-round-trip, security, real-device and operational smoke suite on released artifacts; link immutable evidence and rollback instructions.
cards.security: Close all blocking security findings, retain required notices, verify artifact provenance and perform the final separately recorded security review.

cards.title: Qualify expanded stage broadcast and processing at event scale
cards.deliverable: Exercise the complete multi-instance stage, produced broadcast, audience promotion, encrypted content, recording and captions under sustained and burst workloads. Measure separate interactive, relay, processing and CDN latency/capacity profiles.
cards.acceptance: Independent audience instances receive the correct program and current presentation state. Promotion, processor failure and reconnect preserve permissions and avoid duplicate sound. Published event capacity follows actual results for the stated topology.
cards.tests: Run load and outage rehearsals with real media sources/decoders, authorized processors and broadcast distribution; correlate viewer delay, question/poll timing and recovery evidence.
cards.security: Keep private backstage/conversation content out of the public program and verify key/endpoint admission boundaries under scaling and failover.
external: Provisioned load, relay, recording/transcription and CDN test infrastructure

cards.title: Bootstrap the conference application repository
cards.deliverable: Create the separate application workspace, branded shell, route structure, API boundary, test harness and app-owned plan/handoff ledger. Consume versioned engine interface packages through a dependency lock; keep generic world functionality in the engine.
cards.acceptance: A fresh checkout builds the application against a pinned engine contract and displays an explicit service-unavailable state when backends are absent. No copied engine implementation appears in app source.
cards.tests: Run clean-install, package-boundary, routing and error-state tests. Validate cross-repository dependency/version records.
cards.security: Separate browser configuration from server secrets and apply baseline session, content-security and dependency policies.

cards.title: Connect identities organizations and guest access
cards.deliverable: Implement organizer accounts, organization membership, participant profiles, guest invite identity and an identity-provider adapter. Exchange application identity for scoped engine grants; define session expiry, logout and account recovery boundaries.
cards.acceptance: Registered and authorized guest users can establish the intended identity and request scoped grants. Session expiry and logout invalidate the application session and further grant issuance. C05 and C19 verify revocation of existing connections across engine services.
cards.tests: Exercise a real test identity provider, session renewal, guest reuse/expiry, cross-organization access and logout across tabs.
cards.security: Verify token audience, issuer, nonce and role mapping. Store minimum profile data and prevent a client-supplied organization or role from becoming authoritative.
external: Configured test and production identity-provider credentials where a hosted provider is selected

cards.title: Implement events sessions and schedule persistence
cards.deliverable: Add event/session records, draft and published states, time zones, organizer ownership, session types and links to engine world templates/instances. Implement edits, cancellation and optimistic conflict detection.
cards.acceptance: Organizers can create and publish an event with multiple sessions; participants see only published sessions they may access. Schedule changes preserve stable links and explicit cancellation status.
cards.tests: Test daylight-saving boundaries, timezone rendering, overlapping sessions, concurrent edits and database migrations.
cards.security: Authorize every mutation by organization and event; prevent public discovery of private event details.

cards.title: Implement registration invitations and admission records
cards.deliverable: Add registration, capacity/waitlist records, revocable invitation links and attendee check-in. Support organizer-managed invitations and direct link sharing before optional notification delivery is connected.
cards.acceptance: A valid invitation admits its intended user according to capacity and event policy; duplicate registration is idempotent and revocation takes effect. Waitlist promotion does not overbook under concurrent requests.
cards.tests: Test duplicate submissions, invitation expiry/replay, capacity races and cancellation/re-registration.
cards.security: Bind grants to event and intended identity, throttle abuse and avoid exposing the attendee directory through invitation lookup.

cards.title: Map conference roles to engine capabilities
cards.deliverable: Implement attendee, host, speaker and exhibitor role policies as application-owned mappings to engine join, speak, present, edit and moderation capabilities. Add live promotion, demotion and scoped delegation.
cards.acceptance: Changing a role updates world, media and editing access consistently; a speaker does not automatically gain venue administration or access to other events.
cards.tests: Run table-driven policy tests and multi-service revocation/race cases, including stale tokens and concurrent promotions.
cards.security: Enforce roles on server endpoints and grants. Verify least privilege and prevent role escalation through UI state or modified requests.

cards.title: Build the event lobby agenda and participant directory
cards.deliverable: Provide event landing pages, agenda filters, session details, search, attendee-visible directory settings and clear paths to join available rooms. Display local time and session state without requiring a 3D client.
cards.acceptance: A participant can find the next session and locate authorized people or rooms using keyboard or touch. Private attendee/profile fields remain hidden according to policy.
cards.tests: Test search/filter combinations, timezone changes, accessibility navigation and private/public directory boundaries.
cards.security: Sanitize event/profile content and enforce visibility rules on the API, including search result counts.

cards.title: Connect the venue and shared asset library
cards.deliverable: Expose engine venue templates and organization asset collections in event setup. Support import progress, preview, clone, version selection and quotas using the engine APIs and editor rather than duplicating converters.
cards.acceptance: An organizer can import a venue, track processing and select a published revision for an event. Failed conversion preserves the source and provides actionable diagnostics.
cards.tests: Exercise successful, interrupted and failed imports plus cross-organization asset references and template cloning.
cards.security: Check upload/export grants, storage ownership and private source retrieval; vendor policies do not remove engine capabilities.

cards.title: Build the host venue setup and rehearsal workflow
cards.deliverable: Compose engine editing tools into event preparation: spawn locations, screen placement, stage access, seats, music, environmental audio and prop layout. Add rehearsal sessions and save/publish a venue revision.
cards.acceptance: A host can prepare a complete room, preview four overlapping tracks and wall-video sound, rehearse presentations and publish the tested layout without changing an active session accidentally.
cards.tests: Run setup-to-rehearsal-to-publish tests with saved-world reload and concurrent organizer edits.
cards.security: Keep rehearsal membership separate from published session access; enforce entity-level editing and presenter rights.

cards.title: Build device preflight and join onboarding
cards.deliverable: Provide microphone/speaker/camera selection, audio unlock, network/media checks, quality selection, accessibility choices and desktop/VR entry. Explain actual unavailable capabilities and preserve user choices between reconnects.
cards.acceptance: A user can join with voice only, camera, VR or the accessible view; permission denial and unavailable hardware lead to usable alternatives. Audio starts from a deliberate join interaction.
cards.tests: Test denied permissions, missing devices, output changes, restrictive networks, headset sleep and keyboard-only operation on real browser/device profiles.
cards.security: Do not activate capture before user intent; redact device identifiers and avoid leaking room access tokens in diagnostics.

cards.title: Implement lobby admission room entry and recovery
cards.deliverable: Connect session admission to engine room placement, waiting areas and media join. Implement leave, reconnect, full-room alternatives and clear recovery when a worker is replaced.
cards.acceptance: An admitted user reaches the correct session with matching world/media authorization. Expired or revoked users are rejected, and reconnect cannot accidentally join a different event.
cards.tests: Run multi-client admission races, worker loss, token expiry, full room and network reconnection scenarios.
cards.security: Coordinate grants across services, revoke on removal and prevent open-redirect or arbitrary room-ID entry.

cards.title: Build participant avatar presence and personal controls
cards.deliverable: Expose avatar selection, profile labels, seating, locomotion preferences, push-to-talk/mute and per-source listening controls through engine APIs. Support equivalent essential controls in desktop and immersive UI.
cards.acceptance: Participants see correct identity/presence and hear voices follow avatars. Personal mute, volume and comfort settings persist without changing other participants settings.
cards.tests: Test two-user avatar changes, seat transitions, personal audio controls and XR/desktop switching without duplicate listeners or streams.
cards.security: Prevent identity impersonation and unauthorized avatar asset access; distinguish local mute from host moderation.

cards.title: Build the presentation and shared file workflow
cards.deliverable: Add upload/share controls, screen targeting, slide navigation, looping video, live desktop sharing, presenter handoff and paired-desktop presentation for headset users. Preserve engine spatial sound defaults.
cards.acceptance: An authorized presenter can place content on a wall, loop a video with localized sound, hand off control and support late joiners at the current slide/time. Unsupported files remain accessible attachments.
cards.tests: Exercise slide and video handoffs, capture cancellation, browser audio capture limits, reconnect and simultaneous presenter requests.
cards.security: Validate presenter leases and content access; screen capture uses explicit browser source selection and displays capture state.

cards.title: Build spatial networking and private conversation flows
cards.deliverable: Provide nearby-person discovery, walk-up conversation, personal blocking and explicit private conversation membership using engine spatial media and capability interfaces.
cards.acceptance: Walking between groups changes the audible public mix smoothly. Joining a private conversation requires authorization; leaving or removal revokes media access rather than merely lowering volume.
cards.tests: Test two overlapping public conversations and a private group, with late joins, blocked users and boundary movement.
cards.security: Verify membership and subscriptions server-side, including revoked users reconnecting with stale grants.

cards.title: Implement workshop and breakout orchestration
cards.deliverable: Add creation, assignment, voluntary selection, timed return and host movement between breakout instances. Preserve shared session resources through explicit access links and rejoin state.
cards.acceptance: Hosts can move an authorized group into independent rooms and return them predictably. World state, conversation membership and encryption state correspond to the destination.
cards.tests: Test concurrent assignments, full/failed destinations, interrupted transfers, host reconnect and return timers.
cards.security: Revoke source-room grants according to policy and never transfer private breakout media to other groups accidentally.

cards.title: Build exhibition booths and interactive venue experiences
cards.deliverable: Add exhibitor-scoped booth configuration, shared exhibits, reusable prop placement and guided venue experiences. Hosts can configure animated animals, media walls and sound features using engine components.
cards.acceptance: An exhibitor can prepare their assigned area and interact with visitors without editing neighboring booths. Shared objects and presentations preserve their configured physics and audio behavior.
cards.tests: Run two exhibitor/visitor sessions with scoped edits, saved layouts, walking routes and interactive props.
cards.security: Enforce booth/entity boundaries, object quotas and safe behavior capabilities; do not accept arbitrary uploaded scripts as trusted application code.

cards.title: Build keynote backstage and audience orchestration
cards.deliverable: Implement backstage preparation, stage program selection, bounded audience instances, speaker queue and authorized audience-to-stage promotion. Align slides and interaction timing with live or broadcast delivery delay.
cards.acceptance: Multiple audience instances receive the same program through actual distribution, and promotion creates a working interactive connection without feedback or duplicate audio.
cards.tests: Rehearse program switching, relay failure, delayed viewers, stage promotion/demotion and multiple audience instances.
cards.security: Keep backstage tracks private; grant stage publication deliberately and include relays/recorders in the stated encryption trust boundary.

cards.title: Implement moderated questions polls and audience interaction
cards.deliverable: Add moderated questions, polling, hand raising and response summaries. Associate interactions with event/session IDs and the viewers program timeline where broadcast delay matters.
cards.acceptance: Hosts can queue questions and open/close polls; eligible participants submit according to policy and see accurate results without duplicate counting after reconnect.
cards.tests: Test concurrent answers, duplicate retries, delayed viewers, poll closure races and moderator handoff.
cards.security: Enforce eligibility, rate limits and moderation scopes; sanitize participant content and prevent unauthorized result access.

cards.title: Build shared notes whiteboards and annotation workflows
cards.deliverable: Expose engine collaborative documents as session notes, whiteboards and presentation annotations. Add ownership, save/export, reconnect and accessible editing views tied to the same shared state.
cards.acceptance: Concurrent participants can edit permitted content, reconnect and retrieve the intended final document. Annotations stay attached to the right asset revision and page.
cards.tests: Test concurrent edits, reconnect replay, page changes, export and permission revocation without document divergence.
cards.security: Protect document membership and stored content; reject unauthorized operations even when the client caches a prior document.

cards.title: Build host moderation and participant protection
cards.deliverable: Provide host mute, removal, ban, restricted editing, incident context and participant blocking controls. Apply actions consistently across world, text, media and presentation services with appropriate expiry.
cards.acceptance: A removed user loses relevant access promptly and cannot retain an active microphone or edit lease. Local blocking and event-level moderation have distinct understandable effects.
cards.tests: Exercise simultaneous moderation/reconnect, expired bans, host handoff and attempts to retain stale connections or leases.
cards.security: Audit administrative actions without recording private conversation content by default; prevent cross-event moderation and privilege escalation.

cards.title: Build privacy recording captions and retention controls
cards.deliverable: Expose session privacy modes, admitted recording/caption endpoints, recording status, participant notices and retention/access controls. Support captions in 3D and 2D and manage permitted recordings/transcripts after sessions.
cards.acceptance: A private session has no undisclosed processing endpoint; enabling recording/captions shows the actual trust change. Authorized users can retrieve retained material and deletion follows the configured policy.
cards.tests: Test key rotation, recorder entry/removal, late joins, caption failure, playback authorization and retention expiry.
cards.security: Keep keys and processing visibility accurate; no blanket E2EE claim for material intentionally decrypted by converters, relays or recording endpoints.

cards.title: Complete accessible participation and localization foundations
cards.deliverable: Complete a 2D meeting path with readable presentations, captions, keyboard controls, semantic labels, focus recovery and reduced motion. Externalize interface strings, locale/time formatting and text direction for future language packs.
cards.acceptance: A participant can register, join, listen, present where permitted, use notes/questions and leave without relying on 3D navigation or a pointer. The selected listening policy is explicit.
cards.tests: Run keyboard and screen-reader task scripts, zoom/contrast/reduced-motion checks, long translations and right-to-left layout fixtures.
cards.security: Keep accessible routes subject to the same access and recording rules; do not expose additional private content through alternate views.

cards.title: Connect notifications and calendar delivery
cards.deliverable: Implement an outbound notification adapter, event invitations, schedule-change reminders and calendar-file generation. Connect one selected production delivery provider, with retries, bounce handling, preference controls and idempotent sends.
cards.acceptance: A real test recipient receives the correct invitation/update and calendar times; retries do not send duplicates and disabled delivery is shown honestly. Link sharing remains available independently.
cards.tests: Use a sandbox provider and one authorized real delivery test; test failures, retries, timezone updates and preference enforcement.
cards.security: Protect provider credentials, validate recipients and avoid leaking attendee lists or private session details. Delivery occurs only under configured organizer/user actions.
external: Authorized email delivery account and verified sending domain for live delivery qualification

cards.title: Build organizer administration and operational reporting
cards.deliverable: Add organizer dashboards for session readiness, attendance, room health, storage, conversion failures, usage budgets and exportable event reports. Provide administrative controls through scoped engine/application APIs.
cards.acceptance: An organizer can diagnose a failed join or import and see accurate service health without accessing private media. Reports distinguish attendance, concurrent users and subscribed/publishing media counts.
cards.tests: Test report reconciliation against known scenarios, privacy filtering, stale data labels and threshold alerts.
cards.security: Restrict operational data by organization and role; log safe identifiers and audit sensitive administrative changes.

cards.title: Run the complete conference rehearsal suite
cards.deliverable: Create an automated event rehearsal plus a real participant/headset script covering preparation, registration, keynote, breakouts, exhibits, shared files, spatial audio, moderation and post-event access. Record actual environment and service versions.
cards.acceptance: The complete event succeeds across the declared device/network profiles. Failures become tracked fixes; a passing unit suite cannot substitute for the user journey or actual provider/hardware evidence.
cards.tests: Run multi-client browser tests and real-device/real-service rehearsal with network interruption, media handoff and recovery.
cards.security: Repeat cross-tenant, revoked-role, private-room and recording-boundary cases during the integrated journey.
external: Representative human/device rehearsal participants and provisioned external services

cards.title: Deploy and verify the conference application release candidate
cards.deliverable: Add deployable frontend/API configuration, migrations, secret references, health checks, canary promotion and rollback. Publish operator/admin documentation, self-contained handoff and truthful status integration for the project tracker.
cards.acceptance: A production-like environment serves the application over the intended domain and passes public-path join/presentation checks. Deployment, rollback and restore evidence is attached to the actual commit/version.
cards.tests: Run deployment smoke, migration compatibility, expired-secret, restore and rollback drills through the real ingress path.
cards.security: Review TLS, CSP, cookies, CORS, secrets, administrative access and environment isolation before promotion.
external: Hosting account, domain/DNS access and production service credentials

cards.title: Accept the complete conference release
cards.deliverable: Reconcile every application card, required engine capability, external dependency and release scenario. Publish supported device/capacity/format profiles, known limits, versioned runbooks, acceptance evidence and final progress records.
cards.acceptance: All planned conference capabilities and required expanded engine lanes are verified; no mock provider, unavailable native connector or failed gate is labeled complete. The deployed release passes the final event rehearsal.
cards.tests: Repeat critical production smoke and reference-event tests on the release build; verify links to immutable CI, security, deployment and recovery evidence.
cards.security: Perform a separately recorded final security review and close unresolved blocking findings without weakening required repository checks.
